articles.title: Frank Wynncraft
articles.summary: A Wynncraft YouTuber, in-game name defervesco, a member of Aequitas. His video 'Wynncraft Warring - The Long Raid' (4 August 2024) is the only narrative account of any battle of the private-diplomacy era.
articles.body:
Frank Wynncraft is a Wynncraft YouTuber. His channel, created on 7 March 2024{{cite:youtube-com-feeds-videos-xml-channel-id-uctvz1ej1xkenlaitgsiol3g|channel feed, published date}}, is the source of [[the-long-raid|The Long Raid]] - the only first-person account of any battle of [[private-diplomacy-era|the private-diplomacy era]].

Under the name Defervesco he joined Wynncraft's moderation team on 3 November 2022, introduced as a trial moderator alongside Fleega and Lunatic_Lady and identified in the announcement as "also known as Frank"{{cite:thread-304707|post #1, Mimo, 3 Nov 2022}}.

His upload descriptions carry a standard footer - 'my ign is defervesco', 'guild is Aequitas' - repeated across eleven of the fifteen videos published between February and May 2026{{cite:youtube-com-feeds-videos-xml-channel-id-uctvz1ej1xkenlaitgsiol3g|standing description footer, uploads of Feb-May 2026}}. Defervesco circulated the video on the Wynncraft forums on 9 August 2024: 'Aequitas's claim in sky was under siege for some time last week. Enjoy this retelling of the war!'{{cite:thread-318070|post #1, Defervesco, 9 Aug 2024}}

'Wynncraft Warring - The Long Raid' premiered on 4 August 2024{{cite:youtube-com-watch-v-rlrh14ns6ok|premiered 4 Aug 2024}}, with the description 'Join Aeq for the small guild warring experience!'{{cite:chronicle-records|section 6, video description quoted in full}}. It records a roughly week-long siege of [[Aequitas]]'s claim in the Sky province, and the guild membership is part of how the raid is told: the account is a defender's, made from inside the besieged guild, and the attacking guild was never named{{cite:chronicle-records|section 6, attacker never named in any indexed text}}.

'Wynncraft Warring' is not a series: of the channel's thirteen videos as of May 2026, exactly one carries that title; the rest are build, market, raid and update videos{{cite:chronicle-records|section 6: Frank Wynncraft channel enumeration from the Wayback capture of 8 May 2026}}.

The player does not appear in Aequitas's 135-name member roster of 3 September 2026{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-aequitas|full member roster, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}. When or whether he left the guild was never recorded.

articles.title: FrozenGalaxy
articles.summary: Owner of Aequitas — "Justice Frozenman" in the guild’s courtroom-styled hierarchy — who opened its recruitment thread in January 2021 and led it into Goose.

infobox.label: Known for
infobox.value: Leading Aequitas from its Jan 2021 relaunch into [[goose|Goose]]

articles.body:
FrozenGalaxy is the owner of [[aequitas|Aequitas]] [Aeq]. He opened the guild's recruitment thread on 3 January 2021 and bumped it through that winter{{cite:thread-280525|post #1 (OP), thread opened 3 Jan 2021; posts #4–#5, Jan 2021}}; its rank system is styled on a courtroom, with the two "Justices" of a Supreme Court at the top — "Justice Frozenman [OWNER]" and "Justice Lalatera [CHIEF]" — above Judges, Attorneys, Advocates, Jury and Witnesses{{cite:thread-280525|post #1 (OP)}}. The guild's artwork is credited to Lalatera{{cite:thread-280525|post #1 (OP)}}. Aequitas was founded on 24 November 2019{{cite:thread-280525|post #1 (OP): "Est. November 24th 2019"}}, so the January 2021 thread marked a relaunch of public recruiting rather than the guild's creation.

On 17 January 2021 he added the guild to [[the-forum-megalist|the megalist]] — "Add Aequitas to the list tyvm <3 / Lvl. 48 Community and War" — its first public listing{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #66, 17 Jan 2021}}. By the end of March, Aequitas was inside [[goose|Goose]]; FrozenGalaxy and Lalatera were among the members replying to [[drasalia|Drasalia]]'s Goose fanart of 30 March 2021{{cite:thread-289196|posts #10 and #17, 30 Mar and 7 Apr 2021}}. Aequitas went on into [[khaos|Khaos]] and then [[cucumber-company|Cucumber Company]]{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records: Aequitas membership stints}}.

articles.title: Gavel Reborn
articles.summary: Wynncraft version 1.20, released 20 January 2021, which rebuilt territory warfare from the ground up around guild war towers, a five-resource guild economy, headquarters and taxed trade routes — and abolished territory XP, the economic basis of the alliance order that preceded it.

infobox.label: Introduced
infobox.value: Guild war towers, guild resources, headquarters and trade routes, territory taxes, guild bank, Strategist rank, 4-letter tags

infobox.label: Removed
infobox.value: Territory XP, war servers, mob-wave wars

articles.body:
Version 1.20, titled 'Gavel Reborn', was released on 20 January 2021{{cite:thread-281822|post #1 (Salted), 20 Jan 2021}}{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-1-20|release date}}. Alongside housing, raids and a large Gavel rework, it replaced the guild war system that had stood since [[the-guild-update|the Guild Update]] of December 2014, and is the largest single mechanical break in the history of [[territory-warfare|territory warfare]]. The full changelog had been published two months earlier, on 23 November 2020{{cite:thread-277744|post #1 (Salted), changelog published 23 Nov 2020}}.

## What changed

Wars stopped spawning waves of mobs on dedicated war servers. In their place, attackers were sent to an arena containing a 'Guild Tower' — a boss the attacking party had to defeat — which the defending guild could buff with resources and special abilities at a continuing hourly cost{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Wars' section, 23 Nov 2020}}. Wars were also moved off separate servers into ordinary game worlds{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Other war-related changes', 23 Nov 2020}}.

Holding land now produced five resources — emeralds, wood, ore, fish and crop. A captured territory could be designated a Headquarters, toward which surplus resources flowed territory by territory, and from which upgrades were paid outward across the empire. Guilds set tax rates on other guilds' trade routes crossing their land, could improve individual territories at an hourly cost, and could have their routes cut off by an enemy; guilds could also ally to exchange tributes at a reduced tax rate{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Guild Trading Routes' and 'Diplomacy' sections, 23 Nov 2020}}{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-war|Economy, Guild Headquarters and attack-cost sections}}. Attacking a territory now cost emeralds — initially either the guild's or the attacker's own{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Other war-related changes', 23 Nov 2020}}. Elsewhere the update added a guild bank, a Strategist rank able to buy tower upgrades and territory bonuses, four-letter guild tags, a territory map on the L key, and raised the cost of creating a guild to 20 LE{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-1-20|Changes: Guilds}}.

![Official Wynncraft promotional screenshot for 1.20 showing the in-game Territory Map: connected territories, and a tooltip for Emerald Trail held by the guild Wynncraft giving its emerald and crop production rates.](/images/chronicles/media/gavel-reborn-5e73046b.webp)

The most consequential line in the changelog was one sentence long: 'Territories no longer generate XP.'{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Other war-related changes', 23 Nov 2020}}{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-1-20|Changes: Guilds}} XP became a purchasable per-territory bonus instead{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-1-20|Changes: Guilds — territory bonuses}}.

## Design intent

The changelog stated the goal plainly: to 'allow large guilds to have a stable hold of some territories without needing to play 24/7 to defend it, and also give a chance for newcomers to get started without getting instantly destroyed by a guild with 80 territories'. It also named, in advance, the problem the community would spend the next month arguing about: “We're suspecting the first major problem we'll find will be unbreakable alliances. It'll depend on how easy it is to break those alliances and how greedy allies will be.”{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, conclusion, 23 Nov 2020}}

## Reception

The update landed in the middle of the [[goose-artemis-war|Goose-Artemis war]], one day after the first written use of the name [[Goose]]{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #71, 19 Jan 2021}}, and the warring community's response split along the lines of that war rather than settling into a single verdict.

The first sustained critique came from xMini_ of [[Aequitas]], whose thread 'The Problem With 1.20 Guild Wars' opened on 22 January 2021{{cite:thread-282635|post #1 (OP as last edited 26 Jan 2021; replies begin 22 Jan)}}. He argued that headquarters-distance timers had shut warfare down across the map — 'If we were to try and attack Lava Lake, the timer to start the war would be more than 40 minutes' — and that abolishing territory XP had killed the free-for-all fighting that sustained day-to-day warring: 'Now with the 1.20 wars, there are no FFA's as terrs no longer give xp (another dumb idea). So basically its at a point now where you aren't warring unless you're being attacked.' He also mourned the political order the rework was meant to loosen: 'mega alliances are what made warring in Wynn fun and exciting in the first place. Now that it's gone, a lot of the action and excitement is gone', and noted that subguilds — 'some subs even became their own guild, thus diversifying the warring community' — had lost their function. He wrote from inside the winning bloc: “Look at Goose right now. We have the large majority of the map.”{{cite:thread-282635|post #1 (OP as last edited 26 Jan 2021)}}

A month later _Eragon_, posting for [[empire-of-sindria|Empire of Sindria]], made the opposite argument from the losing side, in 'The Issue With 1.20 Guild Wars': that the rework had failed to break monopolies at all. 'If a mega alliance is already in control of the map then, there is no real chance for smaller guilds to ever hold a territory longer than the cool down… yesterday we were warring in Rymek, and after we had taken 4 territories, the price went up from 4096 emeralds to 24k emeralds.' He added that towers now favoured wealth — 'the only way a guild can reliably take out any guild tower medium defense or above is if that war team is equipped with mythics' — and concluded that 'the guild update shifted from repetitive wars and an environment where it was hard to establish smaller guilds on the map, to an uncreative "build meta" and an environment where it is nearly impossible to establish smaller guilds on the map'{{cite:thread-286375|post #1, 20 Feb 2021}}.

He was answered point by point by [[99loulou999]] of The Dark Phoenix, then in Goose, who defended the system as a diplomatic game rather than a military one — 'Why would a smaller guild hold a territory by themselves if guild wars are a team game where diplomacy is the key?' — and attributed the Rymek price spike to a mass assault: 'every guild in artemis except probably 4 were warring the whole desert/savanah/rymek area currently held by Rays, so its normal that after 5h of constant warring the "pity price" (which nobody understands so far) rose up.' He also recorded the tax settings the community had converged on within a month: 'everyone's tax are on 80% for non ally and 1% for ally'{{cite:thread-286375|post #2, 20 Feb 2021}}. Rothboy of [[Eden]] argued the update had worked as designed — '1.20 successfully made it easier for smaller guilds to get on the map, that was the objective all along' — citing [[idiot-co|Idiot Co]] and [[profession-heaven|Profession Heaven]] holding land under Goose, and claimed the two blocs had simply read the new system at different speeds: 'Goose understood it and got the map asap while artemis failed to understand it and adopted the strategy to wait'{{cite:thread-286375-p02|p2 #26, 20 Feb 2021}}. DeathLucifer of [[thenolifes|TheNoLifes]] dismissed the whole genre of complaint — 'Stop using small guilds as a political tool' — observing that the objectors had not raised the issue while their own side held the map{{cite:thread-286375-p02|p2 #21, 20 Feb 2021}}.

## The war-cost reversal

One criticism produced a change. [[iceresistance|IceResistance]], founder of [[titans-valor|Titans Valor]], opened 'War Costs + Balances' on 31 January 2021, arguing that the update had turned guilds into 'Wynncraft's new money sink': 'In order to participate in the new war system, your members are forced to dish out their own emeralds — as if the new 20 le guild cost wasn't bad enough.' He also argued that the option was self-defeating even for those who used it, since paying from personal emeralds bypassed timers, taxes and route planning entirely{{cite:thread-284184|post #1, thread opened 31 Jan 2021 (OP last edited 19 Feb 2021)}}. He later added a single line at the top of the post: 'UPDATE: This has been changed, and the entire system is completely free to use now.'{{cite:thread-284184|post #1, update line, by 19 Feb 2021}}

The change came in the update's sixth hotfix, which removed personal-emerald attacks, made a landless guild's first attack free, and replaced the flat cost with a scale rising from 256 emeralds at one territory to 4,096 at four or more; the same hotfix cut tower upgrade prices, set a ten-minute post-capture immunity, and required three days' guild membership before warring{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-1-20|Hotfix #6: Guilds}}. IceResistance returned on 24 February to argue that the surviving 'pity cost' — the escalating price charged to guilds attacking a defender that was losing land quickly — had outlived its purpose: 'With personal le warring gone, pity is obsolete.' He reported prices 'upwards 44k+, again before tax'{{cite:thread-286748|post #1, 24 Feb 2021}}.

## Consequences

By removing territory XP, 1.20 removed the thing territorial claims had been for. Under the previous system a held territory generated XP for its holder, which is what made claims worth defending and made the free-for-all hotspots worth grinding{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Other war-related changes', 23 Nov 2020}}; the alliance layer of 2019 and 2020 was built on distributing and protecting that income (see [[the-alliance-wars-of-2019|the alliance wars of 2019]] and [[artemis-goose-era|the Artemis-Goose era]]). Neither camp in the February 2021 argument thought the rework had ended alliance dominance: the pro-alliance critic and the anti-monopoly critic agreed that the map was still held by a bloc, and disagreed only about whether that was a fault{{cite:thread-282635|post #1 (OP as last edited 26 Jan 2021)}}{{cite:thread-286375|post #1, 20 Feb 2021}}. Both [[Goose]] and [[Artemis]] nonetheless collapsed on the same day less than four months later, on 11 May 2021 ([[the-great-collapse|the Great Collapse]]).

The systems introduced here define the modern game: the tax-and-route economy is still the basis of the attack-cost formula{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-war|attack-cost formula and tax rates}}, the ally setting introduced in the same update became the subject of [[the-diplomacy-update|the Diplomacy update]], and patch 1.20.3 of 5 July 2021 layered [[guild-seasons|guild seasons]] on top of it. Compare [[the-economy-update|the Economy Update]] of 2019, which reshaped the player economy but left war mechanics untouched.

articles.title: GaztheCat
articles.summary: Owner of the guild Sequoia. In June 2026 an in-game broadcast recorded him revoking Sequoia's ally registration with Chiefs Of Corkus — a game-mechanical relationship used chiefly to permit joint guild raids.
articles.body: GaztheCat is the owner of [[Sequoia]], the guild founded on 14 October 2022{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-sequoia|guild record retrieved Sep 2026: owner GaztheCat, created 14 Oct 2022}}{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle research notes (2020–2026): Sequoia ownership gloss}} that rose to win seven consecutive [[guild-seasons|guild seasons]] from mid-2024 and fought the [[avicia-sequoia-war|Avicia–Sequoia war]] (2023–24) and the ongoing [[aequitas-sequoia-war|Aequitas–Sequoia war]] (2026){{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records: Sequoia season wins and wars}}.

articles.title: Gilded Sparrows
articles.summary: Gilded Sparrows [Spr] was Killerfish's guild, announced on 17 November 2017 and named as the third guild to join the Coalition. It held mainland territory in the Coalition's November 2017 takeover but appears on none of the alliance's later rosters.
articles.body:
**Gilded Sparrows** [Spr] was announced on the Wynncraft forums on 17 November 2017 by [[killerfish|Killerfish]]: "Founded in the midst of autumn, the Gilded Sparrows flew its first flight through the chilly night sky. And although the guild itself is taking its first steps, its leader is not a novice at what he does."{{cite:thread-208566|post #1, 17 Nov 2017}} The guild had three rules, a joining form and a Discord requirement{{cite:thread-208566|post #1, 17 Nov 2017}}. [[drew1011|Drew1011]] replied the same day: "Good luck with your guild... they grow up so fast"{{cite:thread-208566|post #3, 17 Nov 2017}}. The guild's in-game creation date was never recorded.

## The Coalition

Gilded Sparrows was one of the four founding guilds of the [[coalition|Coalition]]{{cite:community-guild-timeline|Oct 2017 entry}}, the third in order: "It was Fox and Phx that cofounded it, with Spr (the guild Fishie had made) being the third guild to join, and Snt being the fourth."{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L869, composed 4 Mar 2018}} The Coalition's founding dates to October 2017, a month before the guild's announcement thread. Guilds routinely predated their forum threads, so the two dates are not necessarily in conflict, but no earlier date for the guild was ever recorded.

Drew1011 wrote that the guild had one member and that he did most of its warring on its owner's account: "I was also the one doing 90% of the wars for Spr, as Fishie was the only one in the guild and he had given me access to his account to war with."{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L888}} In the same passage he wrote that he had warred on several members' accounts before the practice was banned{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L886–891}}.

## Disappearance

After the founding, Gilded Sparrows was never again linked to the Coalition or the [[the-federation|Federation]]. The guild does not appear on Drew1011's own roster of the Coalition at the declaration of war on 21 December 2017{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L927–941}}, on his February 2018 territory allocation{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L1044–1056}}, or on the Federation's complete member list of November 2018{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}. When or how it ceased to operate is not known.

articles.title: Goose
articles.summary: Goose was the war coalition that rose against Artemis's map dominance in the winter of 2020-21: an unnamed group of anti-Artemis guilds in December 2020, it carried the name Goose by 19 January 2021. It took map control and collapsed together with Artemis on 11 May 2021, splitting into Valhalla and Khaos.

articles.title: Goose-Artemis war
articles.summary: The war for the map that ended the Artemis era, December 2020 to May 2021. An unnamed anti-Artemis coalition erupted against the map-holder alliance, carried the name Goose by January 2021, and fought until both alliances collapsed on the same day.

infobox.label: Outcome
infobox.value: Mutual collapse of both alliances on 11 May 2021 ([[the-great-collapse|The Great Collapse]])

articles.body:
{{map:2020-12-01|The map when the war erupted}}

## Background

[[Artemis]] had been formed on 30 October 2019, in what became [[artemis-goose-era|its own era]], by [[Imperial]], [[Paladins United]] and Caeruleum Order{{cite:community-guild-timeline|30 Oct 2019 entry}}, and transformed across 2020: by March 2020 [[Kingdom Foxes]] was a member and [[ShadowFall]] held a leadership seat{{cite:thread-263975-p02|p2 #36, GoulartJJ, 9 Mar 2020}}, and by December 2020 it was described as 'the war alliance made up of all the current massive land holding guilds', including [[Titans Valor]]{{cite:thread-278112|post #10, Pally, 2 Dec 2020}}. By then its own founders Paladins United and Imperial had drifted out — both were on the opposing side by December 2020{{cite:thread-279337|post #1, Sheepn, 18 Dec 2020}}.

## Course of the war

The war was fought at bloc level, between two multi-guild alliances rather than a pair of guilds. Skirmishing appears to have begun as early as March 2020{{cite:chronicle-records|Goose-Artemis war, originally map-dated from 1 Mar 2020}}, and the war erupted in December 2020 — 913 territory exchanges that month{{cite:territory-exchanges|913 territory exchanges, December 2020}}. In mid-December the opposing coalition was still unnamed{{cite:thread-279337|post #1, Sheepn, 18 Dec 2020}}; the earliest recorded use of the name Goose is from 19 January 2021{{cite:thread-278112-p04|post #71, 99loulou999, 19 Jan 2021}}. In February 2021 Artemis guilds were 'warring the Rays-held desert'{{cite:thread-286375|post #2, 99loulou999, 20 Feb 2021}}.

Goose grew through the spring{{cite:thread-278112-p06|post #113, Lev98bug, 4 Mar 2021}}. By 1 February 2021 ShadowFall, IceBlue Team and TheNoLifes were 'all goose now'{{cite:thread-278112-p04|post #76, urbymine, 1 Feb 2021}} — a side-switch from the Artemis world — and by March–April 2021 the coalition had absorbed the future [[Khaos]] core: [[Aequitas]], Wheres The Finish, ChinaNumberOne, Fuzzy Spiders and Eden{{cite:thread-289196|post #1, Drasalia, 30 Mar 2021}}{{cite:thread-289556|post #1, Drasalia, 6 Apr 2021}}. Goose took control of the map{{cite:community-guild-timeline|the May 2021 entry: Valhalla takes map control from Goose}}.

Amid the fighting, on 25 January 2021, both alliances jointly granted [[Profession Heaven]] neutral status as a public profession-XP guild — a protection that held for five years{{cite:community-guild-timeline|25 Jan 2021 entry}}.

## Aftermath

The war ended on 11 May 2021 when Goose and Artemis both collapsed on the same day — [[the-great-collapse|The Great Collapse]] — reforming as [[Valhalla]] and [[Khaos]]{{cite:community-guild-timeline|11 May 2021 entry}}, whose [[valhalla-khaos-war|war]] began immediately.

articles.title: Guild seasons
articles.summary: The competitive season system added in patch 1.20.3 (5 July 2021): guilds earn Season Rating by holding and attacking territories, with rewards and territory resets every season. Seasons became the calendar by which the community dated its own history, and their winners are the cleanest continuous record of guild dominance.

infobox.label: Mechanic
infobox.value: Season Rating (SR) from holding and attacking territories

infobox.label: Season length
infobox.value: 'Every 3 months or so' as announced; shortened to 1.5-2 months in 1.20.4

articles.body:
Guild seasons were introduced in patch 1.20.3{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|introduced in 1.20.3}}, released on 5 July 2021{{cite:thread-292974|Wynncraft forums thread 292974, '1.20.3 Full Changelog', 24 Jun 2021}}, building on the [[territory-warfare|territory warfare]] rework of version 1.20 'Gavel Reborn' (20 January 2021){{cite:thread-281822|post #1, 20 Jan 2021}}.

Under the system, guilds earn Season Rating (SR) by holding and attacking territories. Territories generate SR every five seconds on a sliding scale that penalises large claims - the fifth territory a guild holds yields only 80 per cent of its nominal rate, and the twenty-second and beyond only 20 per cent - while each successful capture awards a flat amount. At each season's end every territory is reset to the placeholder guild Nobody [None] with its defences, upgrades and treasury stripped, and rewards are distributed by SR leaderboard ranking and by SR thresholds: guild capes, seasonal banners, badges, tomes, emeralds, XP boosts, bank slots, and a crown cosmetic for the #1 guild{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|Season Rating formulas, season reset and reward tables}}. The design deliberately spread rewards beyond the top competitive guilds. The same patch reduced war team size from 6 to 5, adjusted tax caps and added territory loadouts{{cite:thread-292974|Wynncraft forums thread 292974, '1.20.3 Full Changelog', 24 Jun 2021}}. Seasons were announced as running 'every 3 months or so'{{cite:thread-292974|Wynncraft forums thread 292974, '1.20.3 Full Changelog', 24 Jun 2021}}; the 1.20.4 changelog retargeted them to 1.5-2 months, which is why later seasons carry lower winning ratings{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|trivia: 1.20.4 season-length change}}.

A three-day Season 0 ran from 5 to 7 July 2021 as a test, with no banner reward; the numbered competition began with Season 1 on 9 July 2021{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season table and trivia: Season 0}}.

## Season winners

Winners after Season 25 were not recorded{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season table, Seasons 0-26}}. [[titan-times|Titan Times]] vol. 21 (18 May 2026) gives the later calendar without naming winners: Season 28 ran from November to December 2025, Season 29 from January to March 2026, and Season 30 was in progress when that volume went out{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol21|vol. 21, 18 May 2026}}.

Two guilds dominate the table. [[Avicia]] took five consecutive crowns across Seasons 9-13 (October 2022 - August 2023), and [[Sequoia]] took seven consecutive crowns across Seasons 19-25 (June 2024 - July 2025), the longest streak{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season table, Seasons 9-13 and 19-25}}. [[Eden]], despite the claim that it was once '#1'{{cite:thread-206094-p97|p97 #1922, 16 Apr 2023}}, never won a season.

![The in-game guild leaderboard for Season 21, which ended 23 December 2024, during Sequoia's run of seven: Sequoia first on 10,801,762 Season Rating, ahead of Idiot Co, Avicia, KongoBoys, Titans Valor, Aequitas, The Rat Colony, TruthSworD, The Broken Gasmask and Profession Heaven. Published in Titan Times vol. 17, 15 January 2025.](/images/chronicles/media/guild-seasons-5d3bd5b9.webp){{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol17|vol. 17, 15 Jan 2025}}

## Seasons as the community's calendar

Seasons quickly became the community's calendar, and they were fought as alliances — 'our first season being a part of the new Cucumber Company war alliance', Titan Times vol. 1 noted{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol1|vol. 1, 8 May 2022}}. [[Cucumber Company]] was formed for Season 5, which ran from 3 March to 2 May 2022{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season table, Season 5}}. The alliance's rename to Smtn else (later [[smtn elf]]) came 'at the start of Season 8'{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol6|vol. 6, 12 Oct 2022}}, which began on 12 September 2022{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season table, Season 8}}. [[Avicia]]'s Season 12 crown post of 10 June 2023 - the season that ended on 11 June - is the last recorded mention of smtn elf{{cite:thread-308780|Avicia guild thread, season post of 10 Jun 2023}}. Season-end posts by winning guilds are among the era's principal primary sources.

articles.title: HackForums
articles.summary: The dominant power of pre-2018 Wynncraft warring, created on 24 Dec 2014 under owner TheDarkSoul: in September 2016 HackForums held 146 of the map's ~332 territories, and its 2017 peak was reportedly near 350. The Federation attacked its 111 remaining territories on 19 Feb 2018, and by 22 Feb 2018 it held none, ending Hax as a territorial power.

articles.title: Hestia

It declined through 2022, with Adonis founded as its effective successor, and last appears in September 2022.

articles.title: History of Wynncraft guild warfare
articles.summary: A survey of twelve years of Wynncraft guild warfare, 2014–2026: from the first guilds and the HackForums dominance through the mega-alliances, the Great Collapse and the super-alliances, to the private-diplomacy wars whose alliances were never published.
articles.body:
{{map:2018-06-01|The territory map in the Federation era}}

Guild warfare — the contest for the territory map of the Wynn provinces — is nearly as old as Wynncraft's guilds themselves, introduced in [[the-guild-update|the Guild Update]] of December 2014{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guilds|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Guilds'}}. Twelve years of it divide into six eras. The earliest years were documented only on the forums; a continuous territory-exchange log begins in January 2018{{cite:territory-exchanges|continuous log from 3 Jan 2018}}, and from 2026 the game itself records guild ally registrations{{cite:raw-githubusercontent-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod-main-src-test-java-com-seqwawa-|ChatManagerTest alliance-message fixtures}} (see [[territory-warfare|Territory warfare]] for the mechanics and the methodology).

## The early powers (2014–2017)

The [[early-guild-era|early guild era]] produced the first alliances — above all [[Valkyrie]], founded in June 2015 by Kingdom of Foxes and [[Imperial]]{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}} and destined to outlive everything around it — and the first hegemon: [[HackForums]], which in September 2016 held 146 of roughly 332 territories, ahead of the otherwise-unrecorded [[Libertas]]{{cite:pre2018-territory-snapshots|23 Sep 2016}}. Hax's mega-alliance peaked near 350 territories in 2017 before falling; the [[Coalition]] rose in its place, taking the whole map by Christmas 2017{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}.

## The age of the mega-alliances (2018–2019)

In February 2018 the Coalition split, and the [[coalition-civil-war|Coalition Civil War]] between it and [[Alliance Alliance]] birthed the [[the-federation|Federation]] under [[Drew1011]]{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}. The Federation [[the-wipe-of-hackforums|wiped HackForums' 111 territories in under 12 hours]]{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}, grew to some 40 guilds (with the [[Aesir Pact]] inside it{{cite:thread-227373|post #1, OP as edited 21 Jul 2018}}), and held the entire map for 8 months and 25 days{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}} — then [[the-federation-dies|cascaded apart in a single day]] on 10 November 2018{{cite:thread-236962|post #17, Ascended Kitten, 11 Nov 2018}} (the [[federation-era|Federation era]]). What followed was churn: in thirteen months [[SOL]], [[Luna]], [[Terra]], the [[Council of Canyon Kingdoms]] and [[Horologium]] each rose and collapsed, punctuated by the treaties of Rodoroc and Ternaves and Luna's brief total map control{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}} ([[the-alliance-wars-of-2019|the alliance wars of 2019]]).

## Artemis, Goose and the Great Collapse (2020–2021)

[[Artemis]] emerged from 2019 as map holder and transformed across 2020 — its founders [[Paladins United]] and Imperial ending up in the opposing coalition{{cite:thread-279337|post #1, Sheepn, 18 Dec 2020}} that became [[Goose]]{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #71-73, 19 Jan 2021}}. The [[goose-artemis-war|Goose–Artemis war]] consumed the map until 11 May 2021, when both alliances died on the same day{{cite:thread-278112-p07|p7 #134-137, 25 May 2021}} — [[the-great-collapse|the Great Collapse]] — while community alliances ([[Hestia]], [[Niflheim]], the [[Empire of Nemract]]) ran alongside the fighting and [[Profession Heaven]] was jointly protected as a neutral guild{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}} ([[artemis-goose-era|the Artemis–Goose era]]).

## Realignment and the super-alliances (2021–2023)

From the Collapse rose [[Valhalla]] and [[Khaos]], at war from their first day ([[valhalla-khaos-war|Valhalla–Khaos war]]){{cite:thread-278112-p07|p7 #134-137, 25 May 2021}}; [[Vanir]] inherited Valhalla's side and lived twenty days{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. The 2022 realignment merged both worlds into [[Cucumber Company]] — whose 14-guild roster, posted to [[the-forum-megalist|the forum megalist]] in June 2022, was the last public alliance roster ever{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #160, TherapueticLiz, 26 Jun 2022}} — renamed [[smtn elf]] by Christmas{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol6|vol. 6, 12 Oct 2022}}{{cite:cameron-oral-history|Cameron (TAq veteran) oral testimony, fact-checked against map data}}. In June 2023 [[The Aquarium]] and [[Avicia]] walked out ([[the-avocado-split|the Avocado split]]){{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}} and the super-alliance's end was never announced{{cite:thread-308780|Avicia guild thread, season post of 10 Jun 2023}} ([[the-realignment-era|the realignment era]]).

## The private diplomacy era (2023–2026)

Since then, diplomacy has lived in private Discords{{cite:thread-322643|post #1, IceResistance, 2 Oct 2025}}, and the era's wars showed only on the territory map{{cite:territory-exchanges|war windows and volumes, 2023-2026}}: the [[avicia-sequoia-war|Avicia–Sequoia war]], the [[idiot-co-aquarium-war|Idiot Co–Aquarium war]] (the biggest since 2021), [[the-long-raid|the Long Raid]], the record-setting [[aequitas-avicia-war|Aequitas–Avicia war]] of 2025, the 2026 fall of Profession Heaven's neutrality, and the ongoing [[aequitas-sequoia-war|Aequitas–Sequoia war]] against seven-season champion [[Sequoia]]{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season table, Seasons 19-25}}. In June 2026 a machine record appeared, though not of diplomacy: Sequoia's client mod began capturing the game's [[first-machine-recorded-alliances|in-game ally registrations]]{{cite:github-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod|commit 69fb472, 12 Jun 2026}}, a status used chiefly to let allied guilds run guild raids together rather than a record of political alignment{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-2-2-1|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Version 2.2.1' (12 Jun 2026)}} ([[the-diplomacy-update|The Diplomacy update]]). Who was allied with whom, and why, remains unpublished ([[private-diplomacy-era|the private diplomacy era]]).

## Reading this history

The principal records of the period: the [[the-forum-megalist|forum megalist]] (the community's public alliance list, 2020–2022){{cite:thread-278112-wb20210704|post #1, capture of 4 Jul 2021}}, [[Titan Times]] (Titans Valor's newsletter, 2022–2025){{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol1|vol. 1, 8 May 2022}}, the game updates that reshaped warring ([[the-guild-update|Guild]], [[the-economy-update|Economy]], [[guild-seasons|Seasons]], [[the-diplomacy-update|Diplomacy]]), and continuous territory-exchange analysis whose limits are explained in [[territory-warfare|Territory warfare]].

articles.title: Horologium
articles.summary: Horologium was a small Wynncraft war alliance formed on 1 Dec 2019 by DiamondDeities, Titans Valor and The Simple Ones — the last regrouping of the Council of Canyon Kingdoms core. It de facto dissolved on 8 Jan 2020 when Nitrogen2Oxygen disbanded DiamondDeities.

articles.title: House of Sentinels
articles.summary: House of Sentinels [Snt] was a Wynncraft guild founded on 2 July 2016, the day the Kingdom of Foxes was disbanded. It held a seat in Valkyrie, anchored the community alliance Aurelion in 2017, turned to warring, and was the fourth guild to join the Coalition before leaving it for Alliance Alliance in February 2018.
articles.body:
**House of Sentinels** [Snt] was founded on 2 July 2016 by Pyrias{{cite:community-guild-timeline|Jul 2016 entry}} as a community guild, "in hopes of being a place of respite for those who need it"{{cite:thread-135191|post #1, as last revised 29 Apr 2017}}{{cite:thread-187152|post #1, Pretzule}}.

## Foundation

The guild was created the same day [[lovelusting|LoveLusting]] disbanded the [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom of Foxes]]{{cite:community-guild-timeline|2 Jul 2016 entry}}. [[drew1011|Drew1011]] wrote: "After Fox was disbanded, the House of Sentinels [Snt] was created to house the now guildless Fox members. Misty and Pretzule, two ex Fox members, were its leader and Co-Leader."{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L550–551, composed 26 Feb 2018}} He treats "Misty" and "Pyrias" as one person — an identification no other source states outright, though the guild's thread is opened by a forum account named Misty and lists Pyrias first on its council{{cite:thread-135191|post #1, as last revised 29 Apr 2017}}.

## Valkyrie and Aurelion

The new guild took the Kingdom of Foxes' place in [[valkyrie|Valkyrie]]{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L552}}. House of Sentinels was one of the four guilds of Valkyrie's August 2016 relaunch{{cite:thread-147790|post #1, thread opened 29 Aug 2016}}, and Yuno F Gasai answered a rival with "pretzule leads a Valkyrie guild tho"{{cite:thread-147790|post #8, 29 Aug 2016}}. The guild left Valkyrie about 12 February 2017 — "a mere five days after the leadership change", Drew1011 wrote{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L670–671}}.

In February 2017 the guild anchored [[aurelion|Aurelion]], a small community alliance, joining it on 14 February 2017. Its council that spring was Pyrias, Pretzule, wrxryuu, [[killerfish|Killerfish]], ChaChaChaChino and 01100110111{{cite:thread-135191|post #1, as last revised 29 Apr 2017}}.

## The Coalition

In its later thread the guild announced a change of purpose: "Due to a few reasons our guild will also be focusing on warring with other guilds and maintaining territory."{{cite:thread-187152|post #1, Pretzule}} It was the fourth guild to enter the [[coalition|Coalition]] in October 2017, after [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom Foxes]], KingdomPhoenixes and Gilded Sparrows{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L869}}{{cite:community-guild-timeline|Oct 2017 entry}}, and it was on the alliance's roster at the declaration of war on 21 December 2017{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L927–941}}.

## Alliance Alliance and after

On 16 February 2018 the Coalition announced a division of the Wynn province that allotted House of Sentinels "Swamp, Dark Forest, and Rymek"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|screenshot of the announcement of 16 Feb 2018}} — 36 territories{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L1044–1056}}. Within the hour the guild left with [[hackforums|HackForums]], [[paladins-united|Paladins United]], Kangronomicon and [[emorians|Emorians]] and formed [[alliance-alliance|Alliance Alliance]]{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L1057–1059}}{{cite:community-guild-timeline|17 Feb 2018 entry}}. Drew1011 wrote that House of Sentinels made no attempt to raise the dispute with him beforehand and simply voted no{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L1062–1069}}; the guild's own account of that period is not recorded. The guild left Alliance Alliance on 12 March 2018 and returned to neutrality{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L1102–1104}}. It was not listed among the [[the-federation|Federation]]'s members in November 2018{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}, and its later history is unrecorded.

articles.title: IceBlue Team
articles.summary: Wynncraft guild created in June 2015, a co-founder of the Aesir Pact inside the Federation and one of the three guilds whose departure on 10 November 2018 effectively ended it. Warring as Blue Nations United in 2021, it served in Goose, Niflheim, Valhalla and Vanir, and was one of the four guilds whose exit collapsed Vanir.
articles.body:
IceBlue Team ran under three different names and leaderships across a decade of warfare, and is one of very few guilds present in both the [[federation-era|Federation era]] and the 2021 realignment.

## History

### Emperium and Federation (2017-2018)

The guild was a member of the [[emperium-of-wynn|Emperium of Wynn]], listed as 'IceBlueTeam ( IBT) - Owner: orkrider'{{cite:thread-188024|post #1, member-guild roster}}. By 2018 it was led by [[vmark03|Vmark03]] and Mpr100{{cite:thread-227373|post #1, leader table, 5 Jun 2018 (ed. 21 Jul 2018)}}, and it joined [[the-federation|the Federation]] at its founding on 16 February 2018{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, member-guild list, 13 Nov 2018}}.

On 25 March 2018 it co-founded the [[aesir-pact|Aesir Pact]] with [[Fantasy]] and [[sins-of-seedia|Sins of Seedia]], a pact of sister guilds 'especially dedicated to Gavel, and the birth place of Aesir, the canyon'{{cite:thread-227373|post #1, opened 5 Jun 2018}}. Its warring reputation in this period rested on efficiency rather than size: defending the Federation's dominance in April 2018, Goden of [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom Foxes]] cited it as proof that member guilds could still reach the top of the leaderboard — 'that case of more members = #1 isn't always the case, as shown by how IBT took #1 with like four active warring members in total'{{cite:thread-224905|post #7 (Goden), 26 Apr 2018}}.

The Aesir guilds were the Federation's last defenders. A witness to [[the-federation-dies|the collapse]] wrote that after 'fourteen hours of constant warring, Aesir (SDU, DDT, IBT) quit Federation essentially ending it'{{cite:thread-236962|post #17 (Ascended Kitten), 11 Nov 2018}}. IceBlue Team later fought in [[Terra]] from 30 August to 2 November 2019{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}.

### Blue Nations United (2021)

By 2021 the guild was operating under the name Blue Nations United while keeping the tag IBT — 'change [IBT] Blue Nations United to level 82', ran a correction of 14 April 2021{{cite:thread-278112-p07|p7 #125 (ZrBence), 14 Apr 2021}}. Under that name it switched sides in the [[goose-artemis-war|Goose-Artemis war]] — 'BNU(IBT), SHY and TNL are all goose now', 1 February 2021{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #76, 1 Feb 2021}} — and [[drasalia|Drasalia]] drew it as one of six Goose guilds on 30 March{{cite:thread-289196|post #1, 30 Mar 2021}}. It was listed in the only [[Niflheim]] roster ever posted, on 7 July 2021, as 'Blue Nations United [IBT]'{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #146, 7 Jul 2021}}.

After [[the-great-collapse|the Great Collapse]] it joined [[Valhalla]] on 11 May 2021 and followed it into [[Vanir]] on 28 November — then, three weeks later, was one of the four guilds whose departure on 18 December collapsed that alliance ([[vanir-collapses|Vanir collapses]]){{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}.

### Cucumber Company and after

IceBlue Team joined [[cucumber-company|Cucumber Company]] in the spring 2022 realignment but left within months. [[titan-times|Titan Times]] recorded the exit on 12 June 2022: Gang of Fools' 'map claim is the old claim of IceBlue Team [IBT], who have left the alliance and gone mostly inactive. Sad to see them go'{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol3|vol. 3, 12 Jun 2022}}.

As of September 2026 the guild carries the name IceBlue Team again — level 91, 72 members, 15,469 recorded wars, no territories, under an owner who joined in January 2021; when or why the name reverted was never recorded{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-iceblue-20team|v3/guild response, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}.

## Alliances

- [[emperium-of-wynn|Emperium of Wynn]] — 2017{{cite:thread-188024|post #1, member-guild roster}}
- [[the-federation|The Federation]] — 16 Feb – 10-11 Nov 2018
- [[aesir-pact|Aesir Pact]] — co-founder, 25 Mar – 10-11 Nov 2018{{cite:thread-227373|post #1, opened 5 Jun 2018}}
- [[Terra]] — 30 Aug – 2 Nov 2019
- [[Goose]] — by 1 Feb 2021 – 11 May 2021{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #76, 1 Feb 2021}}
- [[Valhalla]] — 11 May – 28 Nov 2021
- [[Niflheim]] — 7 Jul – 18 Dec 2021 (community alliance){{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #146, 7 Jul 2021}}
- [[Vanir]] — 28 Nov – 18 Dec 2021
- [[cucumber-company|Cucumber Company]] — 1 Apr – 12 Jun 2022{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol3|vol. 3, 12 Jun 2022}}

articles.title: Idiot Co-Aquarium war
articles.summary: The biggest war since 2021: Idiot Co against The Aquarium, igniting 29 April 2024 and raging through mid-July with a weekly peak of 5,045 territory exchanges, then a second round from November 2024 into January 2025.
articles.body:
{{map:2024-04-29|The map when the war ignited}}

{{war-chart:Idiot Co|The Aquarium|2024-04-14|2025-02-13}}

## Background

Both guilds had shared an alliance not long before: Idiot Co joined [[smtn elf]] in March 2023{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol9|vol. 9, 25 Mar 2023 — Idiot Co in the map-holding alliance's claim}}, months before The Aquarium walked out in [[the-avocado-split|the Avocado split]]. By 2024, guild diplomacy had moved into private Discords — [[private-diplomacy-era|the private-diplomacy era]] — and the war's causes, its sides beyond the two principals, and its settlement were never recorded. Wider coalitions appear to have fought alongside the two principals, but their names and rosters were never recorded{{cite:territory-exchanges|the wider 2024 coalitions have no written record}}.

## Course of the war

The war ignited on 29 April 2024 and raged through mid-July, peaking at 5,045 territory exchanges in a single week — the highest weekly volume since the wars of 2021. A second round ran from November 2024 into January 2025{{cite:territory-exchanges|ignition 29 Apr 2024, weekly peak 5,045, second round Nov 2024 – Jan 2025}}.

The war spanned the Rekindled World map rework of 10 August 2024, which redrew the territory map between its two rounds{{cite:chronicle-records|Idiot Co-Aquarium war; Rekindled World rework date}}{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol16|vol. 16, 4 Nov 2024 — Rekindled's territory renames}}.

## Aftermath

No settlement was recorded. The fighting faded in January 2025; the next major wars were those around [[Aequitas]] and [[Sequoia]] later that year. Within the war's window falls [[the-long-raid|The Long Raid]] of late July 2024 — a small-guild siege of Aequitas's Sky-province claim whose attackers were never named{{cite:youtube-com-watch-v-rlrh14ns6ok|premiered 4 Aug 2024}}.

articles.title: Kangronomicon
articles.summary: Kangronomicon [Fuq] was one of the two dominant guilds of mid-2015, created in December 2014 and led by Spham and then Dar_Krusos. It co-founded Legio Praetoria, ran a system of subguilds, was a founding member of Ordo Malleus, and was still warring in 2018 as a Coalition and Alliance Alliance member.

infobox.label: Recorded leaders
infobox.value: Spham (to Sep 2015); Dar_Krusos ("Kru", from ~22 Sep 2015); Chawwh (thread owner, 2018)

articles.body:
**Kangronomicon** [Fuq] was a Wynncraft guild of the [[early-guild-era|early guild era]] and, with [[nethers-ascent|Nether's Ascent]], one of the two guilds that controlled the territory map in mid-2015. It was created on 23 December 2014, one day after guilds were released; its creator was never recorded{{cite:community-guild-timeline|Dec 2014}}.

## History

### 2015: Spham and the subguild system

In early March 2015 Kangronomicon was one of four guilds that founded the alliance Legio Praetoria, with KnightOfValor, [[imperial|Imperial]] and Nether's Ascent; Imperial and KnightOfValor left on 5 June 2015 and the alliance collapsed about a month later{{cite:community-guild-timeline|2015}}. Through mid-2015 the guild was led by [[spham|Spham]] — "Being leader of Fuq, we're pretty sure you can get @SSEEBBYZ to do that", one contemporary wrote to her{{cite:drew1011-storytime|forum post by Kuroi reproduced as a screenshot at L25}}. [[drew1011|Drew1011]] later wrote that "Kangronomicon [Fuq] and Nether's Ascent [TNA] were essentially the Hax of mid 2015"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L32}}. A contemporary made the same comparison in the other direction in June 2016, describing [[hackforums|HackForums]] and [[libertas|Libertas]] as a "rule of two" that "many distinguished scholars compare … to the ancient guilds of 'The Nether's Ascent' and 'Kangronomicon'"{{cite:thread-133666|post #1, 26 Jun 2016}}.

The guild ran a system of subguilds. [[holders-of-le|Holders of LE]] became one on 14 August 2015 and was promoted to full ally about five weeks later, receiving nine territories around Nemract{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L96–100, L111–114}}. During August 2015 a glitch prevented Kangronomicon from starting wars at all, and its subguilds were tasked with recapturing anything taken from it{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L34–35}}.

Kangronomicon passed Nether's Ascent in experience to take first place shortly before September 2015. Spham then quit guilds and passed the guild to her senior chief Dar_Krusos, known as Kru, within hours of the change of ownership at Holders of LE on 22 September 2015{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L104–107}}. That autumn the guild came under sustained attack from the [[concordia|Concordia]] alliance; by late September or early October 2015 it held no territory in the province at all{{cite:drew1011-storytime|territory map reproduced as a screenshot at L145}}.

### Ordo Malleus

Kangronomicon was one of the seven founding guilds of [[ordo-malleus|Ordo Malleus]] on 6 November 2015, listed under Kru{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L169–178}}, and appears in the alliance's only recorded roster, of February 2016, as "Fuq, Kangronomicon"{{cite:thread-109350|post #11, 20 Feb 2016}}. Its chief Paladin A'renos organised the alliance's recruitment and created its leader chat, and Drew1011 described Kru as its senior authority{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L155–190}}. After the alliance collapsed on 9 March 2016 Drew1011 wrote that Kru left Wynncraft and "to this day he has never returned, except to pass down leadership of Kangronomicon"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L462–463}}.

### 2018

The guild was still active three years after its founding: a new recruitment thread was opened by Chawwh on 27 February 2018 with the guild at level 56{{cite:forums-wynncraft-com-forums-guilds-72-page-54-order-post-date-direction-asc|guild thread index row, Chawwh, 27 Feb 2018}}. It was allotted 25 territories in the [[coalition|Coalition]]'s February 2018 division of the map{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L1044–1056}}, and left the alliance with four other guilds to form [[alliance-alliance|Alliance Alliance]] — on 16 February 2018 by Drew1011's account{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L1057–1059}}, on the 17th by the community timeline{{cite:community-guild-timeline|Feb 2018}}. Kangronomicon stopped warring around 12 March 2018, one of the markers of the [[coalition-civil-war|Coalition Civil War]]'s end{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L1102–1104}}.

## Alliances

- Legio Praetoria — founding member, early Mar 2015{{cite:community-guild-timeline|2015}}
- [[ordo-malleus|Ordo Malleus]] — founding member, 6 Nov 2015{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L169–178}}{{cite:thread-109350|post #11, 20 Feb 2016}}
- [[coalition|Coalition]] — by Feb 2018{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L1044–1056}}
- [[alliance-alliance|Alliance Alliance]] — from 16–17 Feb 2018{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L1057–1059}}{{cite:community-guild-timeline|Feb 2018}}

articles.title: Khaos
articles.summary: Khaos was one of the two war alliances born from The Great Collapse of 11 May 2021, formed largely from the core of Goose. It fought the ex-Valhalla guilds for a year — peaking in January 2022 — and was defunct by 26 June 2022, its guilds absorbed into Cucumber Company.

articles.title: Khaos's last war
articles.summary: Khaos's war against the ex-Valhalla/Vanir guilds peaked in January 2022 at 500–800 territory exchanges per week and faded to nothing by mid-July. Khaos was defunct by 26 June 2022, its guilds absorbed into Cucumber Company.

infobox.label: Outcome
infobox.value: Khaos defunct by 26 Jun 2022; merger into [[Cucumber Company]]

articles.body:
## Background

The [[Valhalla-Khaos war]] had run since 11 May 2021, the day both blocs formed out of [[The Great Collapse]]{{cite:community-guild-timeline|11 May 2021 entry}}. [[Vanir]] inherited Valhalla's side in November 2021 and then [[vanir-collapses|collapsed itself]] on 18 Dec{{cite:community-guild-timeline|28 Nov and 18 Dec 2021 entries}}, leaving [[Khaos]] facing an opposing coalition that was never formally named — remembered as the Pineapple Pact{{cite:cameron-oral-history|Cameron oral history (TAq veteran testimony)}}.

## Course of the war

The war's final phase peaked in January 2022 at 500–800 territory exchanges per week. The principal guilds facing Khaos included [[The Aquarium]], [[Avicia]] and [[Titans Valor]]; on Khaos's side fought [[Aequitas]], Nerfuria and Eden{{cite:territory-exchanges|principal belligerents by directed exchange volume, winter 2021–22}}. Through the spring the fighting faded steadily, reaching nothing by mid-July{{cite:territory-exchanges|weekly capture volumes, January–July 2022}}.

{{map:2022-01-15|The map at the war's January peak}}

## Aftermath

The war ended not in victory but in merger. Khaos was defunct by 26 Jun 2022, when the forum megalist's final alliance roster — the last ever posted publicly — showed its guilds absorbed into [[Cucumber Company]] alongside their former enemies{{cite:thread-278112-p08|post #160, TherapueticLiz, 26 Jun 2022}}. Ex-Khaos versus ex-Valhalla exchanges flipped from war-shaped to trade-shaped in May–June 2022{{cite:territory-exchanges|the May–June 2022 flip from war-shaped to trade-shaped exchanges}}. No formal dissolution of Khaos was ever announced.

articles.title: Killerfish
articles.summary: Founder of Gilded Sparrows (November 2017), one of the Coalition's founder guilds, and earlier a council member of House of Sentinels.

articles.body:
Killerfish sat on the 2016 council of House of Sentinels, the guild founded by Pyrias on 2 July 2016 and later led by Pretzule; the council comprised Pyrias, Pretzule, wrxryuu, Killerfish, ChaChaChaChino and 01100110111{{cite:thread-135191|post #1 (OP): founding date and council roster}}.

In November 2017 Killerfish founded the guild Gilded Sparrows, announcing it on 17 November 2017 as "founded in the midst of autumn", with a single plain rule: "Be relatively active. After 3 weeks of total inactivity, you will be kicked."{{cite:thread-208566|post #1, 17 Nov 2017}} [[drew1011|Drew1011]] replied the same day: "Good luck with your guild ... they grow up so fast"{{cite:thread-208566|post #3, 17 Nov 2017}}.

Gilded Sparrows became one of the founder guilds of the [[Coalition]] (created October-November 2017), alongside [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom Foxes]], KingdomPhoenixes and House of Sentinels itself{{cite:thread-265297|post #1, community guild-timeline image (imgur seklYAQ)}}. Killerfish's path - Sentinels council member to founder of a fellow Coalition guild - shows that the Coalition's founding guilds were one social circle rather than strangers in a marriage of convenience.

No later roles were ever recorded.

articles.title: KongoBoys
articles.summary: A Wynncraft guild created on 13 March 2021, a member of the Cucumber Company and smtn elf super-alliances and winner of guild Seasons 6 (2022) and 18 (2024). After eight seasons off the map it returned in 2026 and, from 25 May, ran the campaign that ended Profession Heaven's five-year neutrality.
articles.body:
KongoBoys [DUDE] is a Wynncraft guild created on 13 March 2021, owned by hlickyalf as of September 2026{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-kongoboys|creation date and owner, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}. It won two guild seasons, belonged to both of the great super-alliances of 2022-23, and in May 2026 opened [[fall-of-profession-heaven-s-neutrality|the campaign that ended Profession Heaven's neutrality]].

## History

### Inside the super-alliances (2022-2023)

KongoBoys was on the fourteen-guild roster of [[Cucumber Company]] posted to [[the-forum-megalist|the forum megalist]] on 26 June 2022 - the last public alliance roster ever published - alongside [[Aequitas]], [[Titans Valor]], [[Avicia]], [[Kingdom Foxes]], [[The Aquarium]] and [[Profession Heaven]]{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #160, TherapueticLiz, 26 Jun 2022}}. It followed the alliance through its renames into [[smtn elf]], remaining a member from 25 September 2022 to that alliance's dissolution at the end of June 2023{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. Profession Heaven, the guild it would attack four years later, was a fellow member of both.

### Two season wins

KongoBoys won guild Season 6 (6 May - 4 July 2022) with a season rating of 8,168,698 from a field of 169 guilds{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|Season 6 row}}{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-kongoboys|seasonRanks, Seasons 6 and 18, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}, and Season 18 (26 April - 17 June 2024) with 10,651,722 from a field of 277{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|Season 18 row}}{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-kongoboys|seasonRanks, Seasons 6 and 18, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}. Its highest rating of all came in the season after the second win: 12,302,241 in Season 19, finishing with 61 territories{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-kongoboys|seasonRanks, Season 19}} - a total beaten that season only by [[Sequoia]], which won it with 13,480,252, the highest season rating on record{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|Season 19 row}}.

### Withdrawal and return (2024-2026)

The guild's results then collapsed. From Season 21 (1 November - 23 December 2024) onward it finished eight consecutive seasons with zero territories, its rating falling as low as 4,055 in Season 23 and 9,722 in Season 27{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-kongoboys|seasonRanks, Seasons 21-29, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}. The reason for the withdrawal was never recorded.

The recovery began at Season 30, which was still running on 18 May 2026{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol21|vol. 21, 18 May 2026, season dates}}, with ratings of 4,146,687, 6,132,152 and 2,615,532 across Seasons 30 to 32{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-kongoboys|seasonRanks, Seasons 30-32}}. On 3 September 2026 the guild held 32 territories, fifth on the map, headquartered at Forts in Fall{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-list-territory|DUDE holdings and HQ, 3 Sep 2026}}.

### Profession Heaven (2026)

On 25 May 2026 KongoBoys began a sustained campaign against [[Profession Heaven]], running as high as 1,700 territory exchanges a week and ending the neutral profession-XP guild's protected status, held since January 2021{{cite:territory-exchanges|KongoBoys-Profession Heaven exchanges, from 25 May 2026}}. Profession Heaven held no territory at all in the September 2026 census{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-profession-20heaven|territory count 0, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}. The campaign opened during the same season in which KongoBoys' own ratings recovered; whether the two were connected was never recorded. Like every conflict of [[private-diplomacy-era|the private-diplomacy era]], it had no declaration, no stated cause and no named coalition{{cite:territory-exchanges|campaign attested by exchange data alone}}.

## Alliances

- [[Cucumber Company]] - by 26 Jun 2022 (war alliance){{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #160, TherapueticLiz, 26 Jun 2022}}
- [[smtn elf]] - 25 Sep 2022 to 30 Jun 2023{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}

No later alliance of any kind was recorded.

articles.title: Kru
articles.summary: Dar_Krusos, known as Kru, led Kangronomicon from September 2015 and was the senior authority inside Ordo Malleus, where he created the alliance's top leadership tier.

infobox.label: Alliance
infobox.value: [[ordo-malleus|Ordo Malleus]], founding member and senior leader

articles.body:
**Dar_Krusos**, called **Kru**, led the guild Kangronomicon during the [[ordo-malleus|Ordo Malleus]] period. Everything known about him comes from [[drew1011|Drew1011]]'s retrospective account of 2018.

Spham handed Kangronomicon to Kru "mere hours" after the change of ownership at Holders of LE on 22 September 2015; Drew1011 described him as her most trusted chief{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L104, composed 22 Feb 2018}}. Shortly before Ordo Malleus was formed, Kru told Drew1011 that Holders of LE had to elect a council of four officers — a Diplomat, a War Commander, a Community Manager and a Merchant — without saying what for{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L148–151}}; the same four offices were then required of every member guild. Kangronomicon, "led by Kru", was one of the seven guilds at the alliance's founding on 6 November 2015{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L169–178}}.

When a group of leaders wanted alliance business moved out of the chat run by [[arenos|Paladin A'renos]], they took the request to Kru, and he approved the new chat{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L190}}. He then created a further chat named "Shadow Government", which he described as the highest leadership tier in the alliance, one step above the leader chat{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L248–250}}, and it was Kru who agreed to admit [[killerfish|Killerfish]] to it{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L252}}.

When Drew1011 withdrew Holders of LE on 9 March 2016 — the departure that ended the alliance — his leaving message characterised what Ordo Malleus had become: "instead of this alliance being a balance between all the guilds, it become more of a dictatorship between Kru and Arenos". No other account of the alliance's final weeks was ever written.

![The message with which Drew1011 announced Holders of LE's departure from Ordo Malleus, containing the line "instead of this alliance being a balance between all the guilds, it become more of a dictatorship between Kru and Arenos". Screenshot preserved in Drew1011's storytime account, where it is dated to about 5:27 PM EST on 9 March 2016.](/images/chronicles/storytime/15-image.webp)

Drew1011 wrote that Kru left Wynncraft soon afterwards and "to this day he has never returned, except to pass down leadership of Kangronomicon"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L463}}.

articles.title: Kuroi
articles.summary: Kuroi, in game Kur0i, was a chief of Holders of LE from 2015 to at least 2018 — one of the longest recorded tenures in a single guild in the early guild era. A forum post of his documents the 2015 attempt to remove yosteric5 from the guild's leadership.

infobox.label: Known for
infobox.value: The 2015 approach to Kangronomicon over the leadership of Holders of LE

articles.body:
Kuroi appears from mid-2015 and was still among the guild's chiefs in May 2018{{cite:thread-217600|post #1, Thundderr, 10 May 2018}} — the longest continuous tenure recorded for any member of that guild.

Kuroi recruited [[drew1011|Drew1011]] into the guild: the two met in late May 2015 while Drew1011 was seeking help with the Tower of Ascension, and Kuroi invited him to [[holders-of-le|Holders of LE]] the same day{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L15–16}}. Within about a week both were part of a group of members who met at the Troms throne room to discuss removing [[yosteric5]], then the guild's acting leader, from that role{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L22–24}}.

Kuroi then put the request to [[spham|Spham]] of [[kangronomicon|Kangronomicon]] in a forum post — user title "Amateur Quantum Engineer", guild listed as HoL — which reads in part: "'We' being kategajda, @Drew1011, and a few other members, and all of us absolutely despise him … We're asking you to convince our guild leader, @SSEEBBYZ, to kick him out of the guild or demote him … We would have loved to ally ourselves with Kangronomicon, but yosteric pretty much... ruined that chance?"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|forum post by Kuroi reproduced as a screenshot at L25}}

![The forum post by Kuroi asking Spham of Kangronomicon to intervene in the leadership of Holders of LE, 2015. Reproduced as a screenshot in Drew1011's account.](/images/chronicles/storytime/02-a64d84b0a8360b896c510f3abac7132c.webp)

Spham agreed to act only in game, which did not happen; Drew1011 and Kuroi instead raised their grievances with yosteric5 directly and were both made "Head Chiefs", a rank giving them the run of the guild in his absence{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L27–30}}. Kuroi also co-organised the 2015 skirmishes against [[nethers-ascent|Nether's Ascent]] that brought the guild to Kangronomicon's attention{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L31–33}}. Nothing else about him is recorded.

articles.title: l1npengtul
articles.summary: A Titans Valor member announced in May 2026 as Editor-in-Chief of the guild's newsletter, Titan Times, promising a return to a quarterly schedule from volume 22 - a volume that had not appeared as of September 2026.

infobox.label: Known for
infobox.value: Editor-in-Chief of [[titan-times|Titan Times]] from vol. 22 (announced 18 May 2026)

articles.body:
l1npengtul, a member of [[Titans Valor]] [ANO], was promoted to Warlock in volume 19 of the guild's newsletter [[titan-times|Titan Times]] (2 August 2025), where the name is spelled 'l1pengtul'{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol19|vol. 19, 2 Aug 2025, promotions}}, and was among seven members promoted to Strategist in volume 20 (23 November 2025){{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol20|vol. 20, 23 Nov 2025, strategist promotions}}.

Volume 21 (18 May 2026) lists l1npengtul as the newsletter's editor and as a co-author, with DragonZftw, of the main-stage article{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol21|vol. 21, 18 May 2026, masthead and main stage}}. The volume closes with a statement of intent: 'I am l1npengtul, the new Editor-in-Chief for the Titan Times. From the next release onwards, Volume 22, I plan to revitalize and get Titan Times back-on-track as a regular, quarterly publication', thanking 'the existing team of Talkair, DragonZftw, and C0rupted'{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol21|vol. 21, 18 May 2026, closing remarks}}.

No volume 22 had appeared as of September 2026{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol21|vol. 21, 18 May 2026, latest volume held}}. Whether the quarterly schedule resumed is unknown.

articles.title: Lamplesspost
articles.summary: A Titans Valor member, formerly known as thatlamppostguy, who wrote the main-stage essay in Titan Times volumes 16 to 20 - including the November 2025 interview with the guild's owner Calluum on how Titans Valor's leadership passed to him.
articles.body:
Lamplesspost is a member of [[Titans Valor]] [ANO] and was the main-stage essayist of the guild's newsletter, [[titan-times|Titan Times]]. He was renamed from thatlamppostguy by November 2024 — volume 16 introduced him as 'Lamplesspost (formerly thatlamppostguy)'{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol16|vol. 16, 4 Nov 2024}} — having appeared under the old name in volumes 14 and 15{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol14|vol. 14, 24 May 2024, promotions}}{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol15|vol. 15, 5 Aug 2024, Season 18 Ocean Trials}}.

He wrote the newsletter's main-stage essay in five consecutive volumes: on the map's areas in volume 16{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol16|vol. 16, 4 Nov 2024, main stage}}, on what makes a good quest in volume 17{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol17|vol. 17, 15 Jan 2025, main stage}}, on Wynncraft's festivals in volume 18{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol18|vol. 18, 13 Apr 2025, main stage}}, on predictions for the Fruma province in volume 19{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol19|vol. 19, 2 Aug 2025, main stage}}, and in volume 20 (23 November 2025) the interview with Calluum, the guild's owner{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol20|vol. 20, 23 Nov 2025, main stage}}. The interview set out how Titans Valor's leadership passed from [[paladinsorcerer|pally]] to Calluum{{cite:chronicle-records|section 2: Titans Valor succession resolved from the vol. 20 interview}}.

He also hosted guild events reported in the same run - a Wynncraft Kahoot in volume 16{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol16|vol. 16, 4 Nov 2024, events}}, an ironman bingo in volume 17{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol17|vol. 17, 15 Jan 2025, events}} and a location-guessing game in volume 18{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol18|vol. 18, 13 Apr 2025, events}} - and was promoted to Titan alongside Overfears in volume 17{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol17|vol. 17, 15 Jan 2025, promotions}}.

In the guild's Ocean Trials he placed third in guild Season 18 (as thatlamppostguy){{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol15|vol. 15, 5 Aug 2024, Season 18 Ocean Trials}} and third in Season 20{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol16|vol. 16, 4 Nov 2024, Season 20 Ocean Trials}}, then won the 'Champion of the Ocean' title for Season 21 with 1,542 wars{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol17|vol. 17, 15 Jan 2025, Season 21 Ocean Trials}}.

articles.title: Legio
articles.summary: Legio, recorded in full as Legio Praetoria, was one of the earliest Wynncraft guild alliances, founded in early 2015 by KnightOfValor, Imperial, Nether's Ascent and Kangronomicon. It broke up in mid-2015 and was afterwards cited repeatedly as the standard example of an alliance destroyed from within.
articles.body:
Four guilds founded **Legio** in early March 2015 — KnightOfValor [KnV], [[imperial|Imperial]] [Imp], Nether's Ascent [TNA] and Kangronomicon [Fuq]{{cite:community-guild-timeline|undated 2015 entry}} — among the first alliances of [[early-guild-era|the early guild era]]. A 2016 recollection put its size at "2-5 (6?) guilds back when guilds were the newest most popular toy in the playground"{{cite:thread-143392|post #14, Yuno F Gasai, 9 Aug 2016}}. It appears never to have had an alliance thread on the guild subforum{{cite:forums-wynncraft-com-forums-guilds-72-prefix-id-82-order-post-date-direction-asc|complete census of Alliance-prefixed threads, page 1}}.

## History

The alliance was governed by a written instrument. Discussing its membership a year later, a participant wrote: "According to the legio alliance contract when imperial allied with fox they were also a legio guild. But I dont know if those two events happened before, after or in between knv and imp left legio."{{cite:thread-143392|post #17, Yuno F Gasai, 9 Aug 2016}} The alliance Imperial formed with the [[kingdom-foxes|Kingdom of Foxes]] on 2 June 2015 became [[valkyrie|Valkyrie]]{{cite:community-guild-timeline|2 Jun 2015 entry}}; three days later, on 5 June 2015, Imperial and KnightOfValor left Legio, and "the alliance collapses a month later due to internal strife"{{cite:community-guild-timeline|5 Jun 2015 entry}}.

Whether Legio ran community events was disputed on the forums two years afterwards. A poster credited it with the first guild ball; [[drew1011|Drew1011]] answered "First guild ball was hosted by Ordo. Legio never hosted events" and added that he had asked two former members who both said the same{{cite:thread-188024-p04|posts #61 and #63, 22 May 2017}}. Yuno F Gasai replied that "the week I joined Imperial there was a Legio event organized by Knv" and "there was literally an event on the day I joined legio"{{cite:thread-188024-p04|posts #62 and #64, 22 May 2017}}. The dispute was never resolved.

## Afterlife and reputation

Concordia's expansion in autumn 2015 included the destruction of "the remnants of Legio"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L143, composed 22 Feb 2018}} — the last event under the name.

The name was revived once, in secret. An undated plan headed "Plan B/Legio Praetoria v2 — Taking over the Wynn Province" divided the province between seven guilds — [[kangronomicon|Kangronomicon]], Dark Horizon, Gysterium, Necronomicon, [[holders-of-le|Holders of LE]], VerTek and Elevation — with Dark Horizon taking Upper Nesaak, Gysterium Lower Nesaak, Necronomicon Rymek and Holders of LE Almuj. Land was held on condition of activity and forfeit to Kangronomicon or a more active guild if a member could not keep it up, disputes went to [[spham|Spham]], and members were told that "While we're playing the waiting game, not a single word/hint/suggestion about this is to be said to ANYONE" and, if asked what the alliance was called, "just tell them Legio Praetoria V2".{{cite:gdoc-1_p7-wxatmt3am9g|"Plan B/Legio Praetoria v2"}}

In 2016 Legio had become the community's stock example of an alliance killed by its own members. "Legio only lost its territory when it collapsed from the inside"{{cite:thread-130386-p03|post #48, Coronaus, 13 Jun 2016}}; "Legio fell because of internal affairs"{{cite:thread-133666|post #15, Yuno F Gasai, 28 Jun 2016}} — a line written in the same breath as the same diagnosis for [[ordo-malleus|Ordo Malleus]]. The comparison was also used against [[hackforums|HackForums]] at its height: "I gotta admit, legio was well planned. The only difference I see is that hax is more a 1 man allience so they cant really collapse and have internal conflict as easily as legio"{{cite:thread-130386-p05|post #88, Glitchedslayer, 19 Jun 2016}}. The alliance had also drawn a run of hostile threads in its own time: "Why have there been so many anti legio alliance threads", a poster asked in the same period{{cite:thread-130386-p05|post #87, Yuno F Gasai, 19 Jun 2016}}.
