infobox.value: Active; subguild of The Aquarium by 2023

articles.title: Sheepn
articles.summary: Member of Diablo [DXI] and author of "Guild Moderators" (18 December 2020), the pamphlet that made the Artemis war a public legitimacy dispute and preserved the roster of the coalition that became Goose.

articles.title: simplyinfinity_
articles.summary: Leader of Sins of Seedia across the Emperium, Aesir Pact and Federation years; credited as the first to accept the merger proposal that created the Federation.

infobox.label: Known for
infobox.value: Co-leading the [[aesir-pact|Aesir Pact]]; first acceptance of the merger that created the [[the-federation|Federation]]

articles.body:
simplyinfinity_ led the guild [[sins-of-seedia|Sins of Seedia]] [SDU] through several political generations of the late 2010s.

By April 2017 he led Sins of Seedia inside the [[emperium-of-wynn|Emperium of Wynn]], one of the alliance's twelve member guilds, under Emperator [[nitrogen2oxygen|Nitrogen2Oxygen]]{{cite:thread-188024|post #1, member-guild roster, 7 May 2017}}.

In June 2018 simplyinfinity_ ("Simply") and Shy_Phoenix led Sins of Seedia into the [[aesir-pact|Aesir Pact]], the four-guild pact with [[Fantasy]] ([[viaire|Viaire]], SpaseCow), IceBlue Team ([[vmark03|Vmark03]], Mpr100) and [[DiamondDeities]] (Nitrogen2Oxygen, Icey_Diamond){{cite:thread-227373|post #1, leader table, 5 Jun 2018 (ed. 21 Jul 2018)}}.

[[drew1011|Drew1011]]'s "Federation Tribute" credited simplyinfinity_ as the "first consider and accept the proposal of merging our alliances" - the February 2018 merger of the [[Coalition]] remnant and [[war-syndicate|War Syndicate]] that created the [[the-federation|Federation]]{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}. Sins of Seedia later left the Federation with the other Aesir guilds on 10 November 2018, a departure described by a witness as "essentially ending it"{{cite:thread-236962|post #17 (Ascended Kitten), 11 Nov 2018}}; whether simplyinfinity_ made that decision personally is not recorded.

articles.title: Sins of Seedia
articles.summary: Sins of Seedia (SDU) is a Wynncraft guild founded in May 2017 — a Federation-era stalwart and Aesir Pact co-founder in 2018, later a member of Artemis, Cucumber Company and smtn elf, and still active as of 2026.

articles.title: Slayne
articles.summary: Federation-circle player remembered for a November 2018 forum post claiming he co-created Alliance Alliance - and thereby, indirectly, the Federation itself.
articles.body:
Slayne was a player of the [[federation-era|Federation era]]. [[drew1011|Drew1011]]'s "Federation Tribute" credits him among the [[the-federation|Federation]]'s contributors for loyalty and straightforwardness{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}.

Posting in the same thread under the forum title "Tenacious Snuggles", Slayne made the claim for which he is chiefly remembered: "In a way, you could say that I created Fed because I (along with some others) created Double AA. Take that drew! Owait. Im also drew. Damn it"{{cite:thread-237070-p03|p3 #45, 14 Nov 2018}}.

"Double AA" is [[alliance-alliance|Alliance Alliance]], whose split from the [[Coalition]] on 16 February 2018 triggered the merger of the Coalition remnant and [[war-syndicate|War Syndicate]] that created the Federation{{cite:thread-265297|post #16 (Lego_DW), 4 Apr 2020}} - so the post asserts a causal founder's role, jokingly aimed at Drew1011. It is the claim of an interested party: no one else ever named Alliance Alliance's creators, no one contradicted Slayne, and his own wording ("along with some others") leaves the rest of the founding circle unnamed.

His guild affiliation was never recorded.

articles.title: smtn elf
articles.summary: smtn elf was the final name of the merged super-alliance descended from Cucumber Company: renamed 'Smtn else' at the start of Season 8 (autumn 2022), then 'smtn elf' for Christmas 2022, and never changed back. Sixteen guilds strong at its peak, it died in June 2023 when The Aquarium and Avicia walked out, and by August it was gone entirely.

articles.title: smtn elf fades away
articles.summary: smtn elf's last recorded mention is Avicia's season post of 10 Jun 2023; days later The Aquarium and Avicia walked out, and by the 19 Aug 2023 season post the super-alliance had vanished from the record — no death announcement, just silence.

infobox.label: Date
infobox.value: June – August 2023 (end approximated to late June)

articles.body:
[[smtn-elf|smtn elf]] — the continuation of [[Cucumber Company]], and the dominant super-alliance of 2023 — died without an announcement.

## The fade

Its last recorded mention is Avicia's Season 12 post of 10 Jun 2023: "To our other allies in smtn elf... for the hqs."{{cite:thread-308780|Avicia Season 12 post, 10 Jun 2023}} Days later, on 14 Jun, [[The Aquarium]] and [[Avicia]] walked out — rejecting pressure, led by busted moments, to shrink their claims{{cite:cameron-oral-history|Cameron oral history (TAq veteran testimony)}} — and formed the two-guild [[Avocado Aquarium]] pact ([[The Avocado split]]){{cite:territory-exchanges|the 14–15 Jun 2023 ignition of TAq and Avicia's war on their former allies}}.

By Avicia's Season 13 post of 19 Aug 2023 the alliance had vanished from the record entirely. That post instead thanks "The Aquarium - our unwavering ally"; smtn elf goes unmentioned, and no death announcement by any member was ever posted{{cite:thread-310286|Avicia Season 13 post, 19 Aug 2023}}. The alliance's end is approximated to late June 2023{{cite:chronicle-records|smtn elf, end approximated to late June 2023}}.

## A quiet dissolution

The remaining guilds never fought each other: map analysis shows no infighting among the rump through 2024 — a fade, not a violent breakup{{cite:territory-exchanges|no infighting among the smtn elf rump through 2024}}. smtn elf proved to be the last of the public super-alliances; after it, diplomacy moved into private Discords ([[private-diplomacy-era|the private-diplomacy era]]), and no alliance of its scale was ever publicly named again.

articles.title: Snowythewolf
articles.summary: Snowythewolf was a chief of Hall of Fame who opened the Federation's war on 17 February 2018 and called the attack that wiped HackForums two days later.
articles.body:
Almost everything recorded of Snowythewolf comes from one source: [[drew1011|Drew1011]]'s retrospective account of the [[federation-era|Federation era]], written in 2018.

She opened the [[coalition-civil-war|Coalition Civil War]] — "The fighting began with a lone chief from HoF. Her name was Snowythewolf." Having remembered [[emorians|Emorians]]' leaders discussing their low guild bank, she began attacking their Llevigar territories on 17 February 2018{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L1078, composed 30 Aug 2018}}. Two days later she called the attack that ended [[hackforums|HackForums]]: "At the very latest hours of the 19th, Snowy announced it was time to attack Hax. At the time they held 111 territoires. Less than 10 hours later, they had none."{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L1091}} Who called [[the-wipe-of-hackforums|the wipe of HackForums]] was recorded nowhere else.

At the [[the-federation|Federation]]'s collapse, a list of its principal warrers named "snowy" among "the absolute gods of war this alliance created"{{cite:thread-237070|post #18, Lego_DW, 13 Nov 2018}}. She was not among the leaders thanked in the tribute post at the head of the same thread{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}.

A player "Snowythewolf_SP" created [[sins-of-seedia|Sins of Seedia]] on 6 May 2017{{cite:community-guild-timeline|6 May 2017 entry}}; whether that is the same person is not known.

articles.title: SOL
articles.summary: SOL was the Wynncraft war alliance born from the Federation's ashes in late 2018 — the power Luna was explicitly formed to counter on 14 Feb 2019. It last appears in June 2019, with no recorded dissolution; its roster was never published.

articles.title: Spham
articles.summary: Spham led Kangronomicon through 2015, the period in which it and Nether's Ascent controlled the Wynncraft territory map. She took Holders of LE as a subguild, arranged its purchase in September 2015, and passed Kangronomicon to Dar_Krusos on reaching first place before leaving the game.

infobox.label: Known for
infobox.value: Leading Kangronomicon to first place; the change of ownership at [[holders-of-le|Holders of LE]], 22 Sep 2015

articles.body:
"Being leader of Fuq, we're pretty sure you can get @SSEEBBYZ to do that", a chief of [[holders-of-le|Holders of LE]] wrote to her that year{{cite:drew1011-storytime|forum post by Kuroi reproduced as a screenshot at L25}}. Everything else recorded about her comes from [[drew1011|Drew1011]]'s retrospective account, written in 2018.

She declined to intervene in the 2015 leadership dispute at Holders of LE except in game, which did not happen{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L27}}; took the guild in as a [[kangronomicon|Kangronomicon]] subguild on 14 August 2015 after a series of deliberate skirmishes against [[nethers-ascent|Nether's Ascent]]{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L31–33, L100}}; and, when Holders of LE's owner offered to sell it, arranged for her partner unicorn67 to buy it on her behalf. The transfer took place at an announced meeting on 22 September 2015, the guild passing to an account named AALLEEXX which Drew1011 identifies as hers{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L65–71}}. She then made Drew1011 the guild's acting leader{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L71}}.

Kangronomicon passed Nether's Ascent in experience to become the top-ranked guild shortly before September 2015; Spham was online warring when it happened. Within hours of the Holders of LE transfer she quit guilds, giving Kangronomicon to her senior chief Dar_Krusos — in Drew1011's words, "She had accomplished her goal of becoming the best guild in Wynn. She decided to quit while she was ahead"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L104–108}}. She transferred ownership of Holders of LE to Drew1011 in mid-December 2015, by which point she had left Wynncraft entirely{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L312}}. No forum thread, roster or leaderboard names her.

articles.title: SSEEBBYZ
articles.summary: Owner of Holders of LE through the 2015 leadership crisis. Largely inactive, he delegated the guild to yosteric5, then sold it at a guild meeting on 22 September 2015 — the transfer that made Drew1011 its leader.

infobox.label: Known for
infobox.value: The [[holders-of-le|Holders of LE]] transfer of 22 Sep 2015

articles.body:
SSEEBBYZ owned [[holders-of-le|Holders of LE]] by mid-2015 but was largely inactive, having given day-to-day leadership to [[yosteric5]].{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L19–20}} Members unhappy with that arrangement went outside the guild for help: [[kuroi|Kuroi]] asked [[kangronomicon|Kangronomicon]]'s leadership to "convince our guild leader, @SSEEBBYZ, to kick him out of the guild or demote him".{{cite:drew1011-storytime|forum post by Kuroi reproduced as a screenshot at L25}} [[spham|Spham]] agreed to intervene only if SSEEBBYZ logged in, which he did not; Kuroi and [[drew1011|Drew1011]] put their grievances to yosteric5 directly instead and were both made "Head Chiefs".{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L27–30}}

He told Drew1011 he wanted to sell the guild for "5 stacks". Spham declined to lend the money but arranged for her partner unicorn67 to buy it.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L63–66}} At an announced guild meeting on 22 September 2015 he transferred the guild to an account he introduced as his cousin, AALLEEXX — which Drew1011 identifies as Spham's alternate account — after which yosteric5 was demoted to recruit and Drew1011 was named leader in Spham's absence.{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L67–71}}

articles.title: Talkair
articles.summary: A Titans Valor member who wrote and organised the guild's newsletter, Titan Times, from volume 15 (August 2024) to volume 21 (May 2026), and who won the guild's Champion of the Ocean title for guild Season 18.

infobox.label: Known for
infobox.value: Writer and organiser of [[titan-times|Titan Times]], vols. 15-21

articles.body:
Talkair is a member of [[Titans Valor]] [ANO] and was the lead writer of the guild's newsletter [[titan-times|Titan Times]] through its final published run.

He was one of thirteen members promoted to the rank of Warlock in volume 14 (24 May 2024){{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol14|vol. 14, 24 May 2024, promotions}}. From volume 15 (5 August 2024) he wrote the newsletter himself, opening it 'I'm Talkair, and I will be your writer upon this thrilling voyage'{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol15|vol. 15, 5 Aug 2024}}, and he signed every volume from 15 to 21 (18 May 2026){{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol21|vol. 21, 18 May 2026}}. Volume 20 credited him with 'not only writing but organising Titan Times for 5 whole editions'{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol20|vol. 20, 23 Nov 2025}}. From volume 17 he wrote alongside a widening team, handling the cabinet reports and the military-updates section{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol17|vol. 17, 15 Jan 2025}}{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol20|vol. 20, 23 Nov 2025, military updates}}, and he remained a writer under l1npengtul's editorship from volume 21{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol21|vol. 21, 18 May 2026, masthead}}.

Inside the guild he passed the Strategist test in volume 15{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol15|vol. 15, 5 Aug 2024, strategist promotions}} and was promoted to Titan in volume 16, which he reported himself: 'A new titan has emerged! Let's all give a massive wave of applause to Talkair (me??)'{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol16|vol. 16, 4 Nov 2024}}. He won the guild's Ocean Trials 'Champion of the Ocean' title for guild Season 18, ahead of anAlarmingAlarm and thatlamppostguy{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol15|vol. 15, 5 Aug 2024, Season 18 Ocean Trials}}, and placed second to anAlarmingAlarm in Season 19{{cite:titansvalor-org-news-vol16|vol. 16, 4 Nov 2024, Season 19 Ocean Trials}}.

articles.title: tangler
articles.summary: tangler was a chief of the guild Validus in 2015 and the recruiter for its alliance Concordia. On 16 August 2015 he declared hostilities against Holders of LE, and in November 2015 he opened the "Odeus Anti-Validus Pact" alliance thread.

infobox.label: Authored
infobox.value: "Come Join! The Odeus Anti-Validus Pact", 28 Nov 2015

articles.body:
Recruiting for [[validus|Validus]] and its alliance [[concordia|Concordia]], tangler opened contact with [[holders-of-le|Holders of LE]] on 5 July 2015, messaging its leadership after noticing it warring against [[kangronomicon|Kangronomicon]]{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L82–84}}. [[drew1011|Drew1011]] described months of correspondence with him about bringing down Kangronomicon and [[nethers-ascent|Nether's Ascent]], and wrote that Validus attempted to war alongside Holders of LE once, and that tangler "crashed after the very first war and didn't keep trying"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L90–93}}. He added, of the same person, "I still have a lot of respect for him"{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L93}}.

When Holders of LE defected to Kangronomicon on 14 August 2015, tangler added its leadership to a forum group chat and set out the consequence. His post — user title "The Mythical Rebel with Slayer V", bylined 16 August 2015 — reads in part: "I've been saying that Drew's betrayal has greatly limited our options … So, I'm not inclined to try to persuade Ezura to give Drew another chance, and will act on his instructions accordingly. What a waste, now we all get to fight while TNA laughs . . . I give you an hour's notice, an hour more than Drew gave me."{{cite:drew1011-storytime|forum post by tangler, dated 16 Aug 2015, reproduced as a screenshot at L96}} The upper half of the same post quotes Ezura, Validus's leader, reacting to the defection; Drew1011 wrote that the quotation "was later revealed" to have been edited from an unrelated exchange{{cite:drew1011-storytime|L97}}.

![The upper half of tangler's forum post of 16 August 2015, carrying a quotation attributed to Ezura about Holders of LE's defection; Drew1011 wrote that the quotation had been edited from an exchange on a different subject.](/images/chronicles/storytime/03-image.webp)

On 28 November 2015 he opened the thread "Come Join! The Odeus Anti-Validus Pact"; it ran to 24 replies and 5,259 views before being locked, the moderator Mekyr making its last post on 29 November 2015{{cite:forums-wynncraft-com-forums-guilds-72-prefix-id-82-order-post-date-direction-asc|Alliance-prefix thread index}}. The thread's text does not survive, and why a Validus chief authored a pact named against his own guild was never recorded.

articles.title: Tapu_Fini
articles.summary: Founder of The Separatists in June 2016 and, under his earlier username Supermariowifi, leader of its founding guild The Anarchy. His opening post is the earliest written account of the HackForums–Libertas "rule of two".

articles.title: Terra
articles.summary: Terra was a short-lived Wynncraft war alliance of autumn 2019 — the bloc that broke Luna's total map control. Formed on 30 Aug 2019, it took the map on 8 Sep after The Simple Ones defected to it, and fell on 2 Nov 2019, its fragments launching one final raid on the newborn Artemis on 10 Nov.

articles.title: Terra falls
articles.summary: Terra, the alliance that broke Luna, fell on 2 Nov 2019 — seven weeks after its victory. On 10 Nov its fragments launched one last raid on the newborn Artemis.
articles.body:
[[Terra]] formed on 30 Aug 2019 in opposition to [[Luna]] and took the map from it on 8 Sep, after The Simple Ones' defection ([[Luna-Terra war]]){{cite:community-guild-timeline|30 Aug and 8 Sep 2019 entries}}. Its own end began almost immediately.

## The dispersal

Victory scattered the bloc in stages. On 15 Sep 2019 its core — [[Kingdom Foxes]], [[DiamondDeities]], [[Titans Valor]], [[The Simple Ones]], [[Fantasy]], Phantom Hearts and Empire of Sindria — left to found the [[Council of Canyon Kingdoms]]{{cite:community-guild-timeline|15 Sep 2019 entry}}. Paladins United departed on 30 Oct to co-found [[Artemis]]{{cite:community-guild-timeline|30 Oct 2019 entry}}. What remained was a rump: chronicle stints place Lunatic, IceBlue Team, Achte Shadow and FinalFront in Terra to the start of November{{cite:territory-exchanges|the rump roster's activity windows, autumn 2019}}.

The community guild-timeline records the end simply: "November 2nd 2019 Terra 'falls'" — the quotation marks are in the original{{cite:thread-265297|post #1, the community guild-timeline image}}, and no fuller dissolution statement survives.

## The last raid

On 10 Nov 2019 Terra's fragments launched one final raid on the newborn Artemis, eleven days old. It was the bloc's last recorded act{{cite:thread-265297|post #1, the community guild-timeline image}}; its guilds then dispersed into the winter's realignments.

{{map:2019-11-02|The map when Terra fell}}

articles.title: Territory warfare
articles.summary: How Wynncraft guild wars work — territories, wars before and after the 1.20 rework, seasons, FFA hotspots and ally territory-trading — and why raw exchange volume is not evidence of war.
articles.body:
Wynncraft's provinces are divided into territories that guilds capture and hold. Territory warfare has existed since [[the-guild-update|the Guild Update]] of December 2014{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guilds|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Guilds'}}, in two mechanical epochs.

## The two war systems

In the original system (2014–2021), wars spawned waves of mobs on dedicated war servers and territories generated XP for their holders{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Guilds & Wars' sections, 23 Nov 2020}}. Version 1.20 'Gavel Reborn' (20 January 2021){{cite:thread-281822|post #1, 20 Jan 2021}} rebuilt it: attacking now costs guild emeralds and is resolved by defeating the territory's war tower; territories produce resources moved along trade routes, can be taxed (including a separate ally tax), and support a headquarters whose strength scales with connected holdings{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Guilds & Wars' sections, 23 Nov 2020}}{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-war|Economy and Guild Headquarters sections; ally tax rate in the attack-cost formula}}. Patch 1.20.3 (5 July 2021) added [[guild-seasons|guild seasons]] — Season Rating earned by holding and attacking territories, with resets and rewards every season{{cite:thread-292974|Wynncraft forums thread 292974, '1.20.3 Full Changelog', 24 Jun 2021}}{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|Season Rating formulas and season reset}} — which turned holding land into a scheduled competition.

![In-game screenshot of a standard guild war arena, the instanced combat space a player enters when attacking a territory's war tower under the post-1.20 system.](/images/chronicles/media/territory-warfare-c603561e.webp)

## Reading the exchange record

The territory_exchanges log has run continuously since 3 January 2018{{cite:territory-exchanges|continuous log from 3 Jan 2018}}. Raw exchange volume is not evidence of war: two phenomena generate enormous exchange counts in peacetime.

- **FFA hotspots** — clusters that churn perpetually regardless of politics, such as Detlas, the Hive, Lava Lake, Factory Entrance and the Emerald Trail, joined in 2020–21 by the Silent Expanse{{cite:chronicle-map-methodology|FFA hotspot list: Detlas, Hive, Lava Lake, Factory Entrance, Emerald Trail, Silent Expanse}}. Fighting concentrated on these territories is noise, not campaign{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-war|Glossary: 'free for alls are not officially recognised'}}.
- **Ally territory-trading** — from the 1.20 era, allied guilds mass-trade territories for XP and SR, producing near-symmetric exchange counts (Avicia and Emorians once traded roughly 5,000 captures each way while allied){{cite:chronicle-map-methodology|ally territory-trading: Avicia-Emorians ~5k each way, 76% on FFA/Silent Expanse, near-perfect symmetry}}.

![Annotated territory map of the Jungle FFA introduced in guild Season 17, published in Titan Times vol. 13 (22 March 2024): map squares labelled with the holding guild's tag - TAq, ANO, BFS, AVO - and numbered in attack order.](/images/chronicles/media/territory-warfare-1c6832fa.webp){{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol13|vol. 13, 22 Mar 2024}}

A real war instead shows spread and asymmetry: sustained fighting across 100+ territories with a low share on FFA hotspots. Territory-exchange figures in these articles therefore count captures outside the FFA hotspots, and bloc rosters inferred from co-belligerence are inference, never recorded fact{{cite:chronicle-map-methodology|war criteria: real wars span 100+ territories with low FFA concentration}}. In the [[goose-artemis-war|Goose]] roster episode, a map-inferred roster initially contradicted the written record{{cite:chronicle-map-methodology|Goose roster 'ENTIRELY MAP-INFERRED' note}}.

articles.title: The 2026 territory map
articles.summary: A complete snapshot of Wynncraft's guild map taken from the game's API on 3 September 2026: 437 territories held by 20 guilds, four of which held more than half the map between them. It is the most complete documented state of the map in an era when almost nothing else about guild politics was written down.
articles.body:
{{map:2026-09-01|The territory map in September 2026}}

The census matters chiefly as documentation{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-list-territory|full territory ownership snapshot, 3 Sep 2026}}. By 2026 no guild published an alliance roster, no newsletter named an enemy and no war carried a declaration{{cite:chronicle-records|sections 1 and 8: the silence of 2023-2026}}, so a machine capture of who held what is the fullest single statement of guild politics available for [[private-diplomacy-era|the private-diplomacy era]].

## The census

| Territories | Guild | Tag | Headquarters |
|---|---|---|---|
| 62 | [[Sequoia]] | SEQ | Corrupted Warfront |
| 59 | [[the-nameless-samurai|The Nameless Samurai]] | TNSR | Cinfras Outskirts |
| 59 | [[Avicia]] | AVO | Bloody Trail |
| 55 | [[Kingdom Foxes]] | Fox | Bandit's Toll |
| 32 | [[KongoBoys]] | DUDE | Forts in Fall |
| 31 | [[Titans Valor]] | ANO | Nodguj Nation |
| 25 | Empire of Sindria | ESI | Corkus City |
| 22 | [[Aequitas]] | Aeq | Mount Wynn Inn |
| 21 | New Moon | NewM | Almuj |
| 21 | [[Paladins United]] | PUN | Central Islands |
| 12 | Pavilion | PAV | Toxic Drip |
| 9 | PotatoSigmas | pots | Apprentice Huts |
| 8 | Black Fangs | BFS | Azure Frontier |
| 6 | Clear Skies | Skye | Pyroclastic Flow |
| 6 | Angels Of Eternal | AoE | Waterfall Cave |
| 5 | Empire of TKW | ETKW | Unicorn Trail |
| 1 | Censing Market | CENS | Big Mushroom Cave |
| 1 | gugu gaga | Cgua | Swamp Island |
| 1 | TheButteryWarriors | TBUH | Little Wood |
| 1 | Wynnpelago | APgg | Lion Lair |

The map was concentrated: the four largest holders controlled 235 territories between them, 53.8 per cent of the map, and the top ten controlled 387, or 88.6 per cent{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-list-territory|counts computed from the 3 Sep 2026 snapshot}}.

## The principal holders

Guild records captured from the same API ninety seconds before the census give owners and founding dates for the ten largest holders{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-sequoia|guild record, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-the-20nameless-20samurai|guild record, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-avicia|guild record, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-kingdom-20foxes|guild record, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-kongoboys|guild record, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-titans-20valor|guild record, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-empire-20of-20sindria|guild record, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-aequitas|guild record, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-new-20moon|guild record, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-paladins-20united|guild record, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}:

| Guild | Owner | Created | Lifetime wars |
|---|---|---|---|
| [[Sequoia]] | [[gazthecat|GaztheCat]] | 14 Oct 2022 | 161,494 |
| [[the-nameless-samurai|The Nameless Samurai]] | makugon | 28 Sep 2023 | 12,345 |
| [[Avicia]] | Krokofant | 1 Aug 2018 | 227,706 |
| [[Kingdom Foxes]] | SpaseCow | 3 Jul 2016 | 22,356 |
| [[KongoBoys]] | hlickyalf | 13 Mar 2021 | 98,864 |
| [[Titans Valor]] | Calluum | 2 Jul 2017 | 119,437 |
| Empire of Sindria | xNova204 | 18 Mar 2019 | 69,059 |
| [[Aequitas]] | [[frozengalaxy|Frozenman]] | 24 Nov 2019 | 177,498 |
| New Moon | zyX_01 | 12 May 2025 | 7,860 |
| [[Paladins United]] | Zinnig | 2 Jun 2017 | 33,819 |

The list spans the whole history of the game's guild warfare. Kingdom Foxes was created in July 2016 and Paladins United and Titans Valor in mid-2017, all three survivors of [[early-guild-era|the early guild era]] still holding land a decade later. At the other end, New Moon was created in May 2025 and The Nameless Samurai in September 2023; nothing was ever written about either.

Three guilds with very large lifetime war counts held nothing at all: [[The Aquarium]] (170,247 wars){{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-the-20aquarium|territory count 0, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}, [[Idiot Co]] (126,366){{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-idiot-20co|territory count 0, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}} and [[Profession Heaven]]{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-profession-20heaven|territory count 0, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}. All three had won or contended for seasons in 2023-24{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|Seasons 14, 15 and 17}}; why they left the map was never recorded.

## How little a snapshot is

The census carries an acquisition timestamp for every territory, and they show how provisional any map picture of this period is. No territory in the capture had been held for as long as a week: the longest-held had changed hands 144 hours earlier, the median holding was 11 hours old, 268 of the 437 had been taken within the previous day and 104 within the previous hour{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-list-territory|acquisition timestamps, computed against the capture time of 3 Sep 2026 17:00 UTC}}.

The drift is visible even inside a single archiving run. The per-guild records were fetched at 16:59 UTC and the census at 17:00 UTC, ninety-three seconds later, and in that gap Sequoia's holdings fall from 63 to 62 and Aequitas's rise from 21 to 22{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-sequoia|territories field, retrieved 3 Sep 2026 16:59 UTC}}{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-aequitas|territories field, retrieved 3 Sep 2026 16:59 UTC}}{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-list-territory|SEQ and Aeq counts, 3 Sep 2026 17:00 UTC}}. The census is a state of the map at one minute, not a settlement.

## What the map does not show

It does not show who was allied with whom. No alliance roster was published after June 2022{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #160, TherapueticLiz, 26 Jun 2022}}, and the in-game ally registrations that became machine-readable in June 2026 record a game-mechanical relationship used chiefly to permit allied guilds to run guild raids together - not political alignment, and no guide to the blocs behind the map{{cite:raw-githubusercontent-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod-main-src-test-java-com-seqwawa-|ChatManagerTest alliance-message fixtures}}{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-war|ally tax rate in the attack-cost formula}}. Nor does it show causes: of the guilds in the table, Sequoia, Avicia and Aequitas fought wars in this period that no one described in writing{{cite:territory-exchanges|2023-2026 war windows}}, and for The Nameless Samurai, Kingdom Foxes, New Moon and the smaller holders no narrative of any kind was ever recorded.

articles.title: The alliance wars of 2019
articles.summary: The churn year after the Federation's fall: SOL, Luna, Terra, the Council of Canyon Kingdoms and Horologium all rose and collapsed within thirteen months, ending with the disbanding of DiamondDeities in January 2020.
articles.body:
{{map:2019-09-10|The map during the Luna–Terra war}}

No alliance formed in 2019 survived the year intact. Between the [[the-federation-dies|Federation's death]] in November 2018 and the disbanding of [[DiamondDeities]] in January 2020, five successive alliances rose to power and collapsed.

## SOL and the founding of Luna

[[SOL]] was created in the chaos after the Federation's fall in late 2018{{cite:thread-265297|post #1, community guild-timeline image (imgur seklYAQ), 28 Jul 2020}}{{cite:thread-251543|post #1, Pikacal, 26 Jun 2019}}. Its roster was never published; its members appear to have been DiamondDeities, Achte Shadow, Wrath Of Poseidon, Beyond the Scene, Spectral Cabbage and, later, Ecliptic Awakening{{cite:territory-exchanges|SOL roster inferred from co-belligerence, labelled inference}}. It became the power that [[Luna]] was explicitly formed to counter on 14 February 2019, by [[Imperial]], [[Emorians]], Blacklisted, BuildCraftia and others{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. [[Kingdom Foxes]] was not a Luna founder — Luna was at war with Fox from its second day, a war fought across 300+ territories in which Imperial alone attacked Fox 660 times{{cite:territory-exchanges|Luna-Kingdom Foxes war, Feb-Jul 2019}}. By 3 March 2019 the front-runners were Imperial with 85 territories and Emorians with 61{{cite:pre2018-territory-snapshots|3 Mar 2019}}. The war ended when Fox joined Luna on 8 July 2019, the day after the Treaty of Ternaves (signed by Fox, [[The Simple Ones]] and ThisIsMurica, splitting the territory of the dissolved Celestial Tigers); the earlier Treaty of Rodoroc (effective 2 March 2019) had already made peace between Fox and DiamondDeities{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. SOL itself appears to have dissolved by mid-2019 as Luna consolidated.

## Luna's map — and Luna's fall

After fending off an attack on Kingdom Foxes, Luna wiped every guild but [[Avicia]]; Avicia joined on 17 July 2019 and Luna held the entire map{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. Six weeks later it tore itself apart: on 29 August 2019, after a leadership dispute, Emorians and Avicia left and declared war on Imperial, ThisIsMurica was kicked the next day for sending fighters, and [[Terra]] formed in the chaos on 30 August. The war for the map ran 7–19 September — over 2,000 exchanges across 322 territories in ten days{{cite:territory-exchanges|Luna-Terra war window, 6-16 Sep 2019: 2,174 attacks across 322 territories}}. The Simple Ones defected to Terra on 8 September and Terra took map control the same day; Kingdom Foxes left on the 18th and Luna collapsed{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}.

## A participant's account

The fullest narrative of the year's politics is a memoir chapter, "Recent Wynncraft Guild History", written by [[arkada|Arkada]] — Leonhart_Arkada, an Aedile of [[Titans Valor]]{{cite:thread-252647|post #1, Leonhart_Arkada, 20 Jul 2019}} — and published on 14 September 2019, while the fighting was still going on{{cite:wattpad-com-784189853-inside-myself-recent-wynncraft-guild-history|chapter "Recent Wynncraft Guild History", 14 Sep 2019}}. Written from the Terra side, it compresses the chronology in places; it is the only near-contemporaneous account of the war's politics, the sole witness for some events, and several of its details are corroborated by the map data.

Arkada frames Luna not as a new alliance but as a renamed old one: "The Valkyrie alliance, consisting of Kingdom Foxes, Imperial, Paladins United, and Emorians" crushed a summer raid on Kingdom Foxes, invaded every opposing alliance's land in under two days, and thereafter appears as "the Valkyrie alliance, now calling themselves the Luna alliance"{{cite:wattpad-com-784189853-inside-myself-recent-wynncraft-guild-history|chapter "Recent Wynncraft Guild History", 14 Sep 2019}}. He attributes the raid's failure to Valkyrie's "controversial use of sub guilds", which let main-guild members defend land faster. Blacklisted and BuildCraftia defected to the winning side, then Avicia and The Simple Ones{{cite:wattpad-com-784189853-inside-myself-recent-wynncraft-guild-history|chapter "Recent Wynncraft Guild History", 14 Sep 2019}}.

The revolt that broke Luna had a political mechanism: the Emorians left "frustrated with the actions of other prominent guilds", and Luna then "seized all of its lands" — "a large mistake", in Arkada's judgement, because it made the Emorians sympathetic to the resistance. Terra was a merger of several small anti-Luna alliances — his own guild had been fighting in one called The Ascendancy — that assembled "nearly 15 guilds" for the weekend raid on Imperial and wiped every Luna guild but Kingdom Foxes in about six hours. On 14 September 2019 Luna mounted a counter-raid, forewarned by a spy, which Terra repelled: "Luna could not progress, and we considered their raid a failure."{{cite:wattpad-com-784189853-inside-myself-recent-wynncraft-guild-history|chapter "Recent Wynncraft Guild History", 14 Sep 2019}}

## Victors without peace

Terra's core founded the [[Council of Canyon Kingdoms]] on 15 September 2019 — Kingdom Foxes, DiamondDeities, Titans Valor, The Simple Ones, [[Fantasy]], Phantom Hearts and Empire of Sindria{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. On 30 October, Imperial, [[Paladins United]] and Caeruleum Order founded [[Artemis]]. Terra fell on 2 November, seven weeks after its victory, its fragments launching one last raid on the newborn Artemis on 10 November{{cite:thread-265297|post #1, community guild-timeline image (imgur seklYAQ), 28 Jul 2020}}. The Council collapsed on 23 November when The Ascendancy bloc departed. On 1 December, DiamondDeities, Titans Valor and The Simple Ones formed [[Horologium]]{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}} — the year's last alliance.

## The end of the churn

On 8 January 2020, [[Nitrogen2Oxygen]] disbanded DiamondDeities, taking Horologium down with it; most remaining members regrouped as Lux Nova the next day{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. Of the year's combatants only Artemis remained standing — the map-holder of the coming [[artemis-goose-era|Artemis–Goose era]].

articles.title: The Aquarium
articles.summary: Wynncraft guild founded in March 2020, active in territory warfare from its first days. A founding member of Valhalla and Vanir, a member of Cucumber Company and smtn elf, half of the Avocado Aquarium pact, and a principal in the 2024-25 Idiot Co-Aquarium war, the biggest war since 2021.

articles.title: The Avocado split
articles.summary: The Aquarium and Avicia quit the smtn elf super-alliance in June 2023, rejecting pressure to shrink their claims, then waged a sniping and claim-taking campaign against their former allies into early 2024 as the two-guild Avocado Aquarium pact.

infobox.label: Belligerents
infobox.value: [[Avocado Aquarium]] ([[The Aquarium]], [[Avicia]]) vs their former [[smtn elf]] allies

infobox.label: Outcome
infobox.value: No settlement recorded; the campaign faded in early 2024 and smtn elf dissolved

articles.body:
{{map:2023-06-14|The map when TAq and Avicia walked out}}

## Background

smtn elf was the direct continuation of [[Cucumber Company]]{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol6|vol. 6, 12 Oct 2022 — "Cucumber was archived. The new alliance name is called 'Smtn else'"}}, the mega-bloc of [[the-realignment-era|the 2022 realignment]] — called 'unquestionably the greatest super-alliance of 2023' in a February 2023 thread. Pressure inside the alliance — led by busted moments, a member since March 2023{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol9|vol. 9, 25 Mar 2023 — [fuy] joined the map-holding alliance mid-season}} — for The Aquarium and Avicia to shrink their claims drove the two guilds out{{cite:cameron-oral-history|Cameron oral history (TAq veteran testimony)}}.

## Course of the war

The Aquarium and Avicia quit in mid-June 2023; their war on their former allies ignited on 14–15 June{{cite:territory-exchanges|the 14–15 Jun 2023 ignition of TAq and Avicia's war on their former allies}}. As a two-guild pact they waged a sniping and claim-taking campaign, running mega-claims across TAq, AVO and their subguilds ShadowFall, the Avos, and the joint subguild Avoquarium [HQs], created 9 August 2023{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-avoquarium|Wynncraft API v3 guild record: Avoquarium [HQs], created 9 Aug 2023}}. By August 2023 the two were each other's 'unwavering ally'{{cite:thread-310286|Avicia Season 13 post, 19 Aug 2023}}.

The name 'Avocado Aquarium' was never written down at the time{{cite:cameron-oral-history|Cameron oral history (TAq veteran testimony)}}, and the pact announced nothing publicly. Its opponent was the multi-guild smtn elf rump, not a single guild.

## Aftermath

smtn elf did not survive the walkout. It was last mentioned in Avicia's Season 12 post of 10 June 2023{{cite:thread-308780|Avicia Season 12 post, 10 Jun 2023}}; by the Season 13 post of 19 August 2023 it was gone, its dissolution never announced{{cite:thread-310286|Avicia Season 13 post, 19 Aug 2023}}. The remaining guilds never fought each other.

The Avocado campaign faded in early 2024; the pact appears to have ended in late February. The first friction between The Aquarium and Avicia themselves came only in June 2024{{cite:territory-exchanges|first TAq-Avicia friction, June 2024}}, after the pact — by which time [[idiot-co-aquarium-war|the biggest war since 2021]] had begun. The split marks the start of [[private-diplomacy-era|the private-diplomacy era]]: no bloc roster of 2023–2026 was ever published.

articles.title: The betrayal of Valhalla
articles.summary: The Mage Legacy and TheNoLifes turned on their Valhalla allies — friction visible from August 2021, erupting into open war in December with 5,359 territory exchanges that month. Both were excluded when Vanir formed on 28 Nov 2021.

infobox.label: Belligerents
infobox.value: The Mage Legacy, TheNoLifes vs the [[Valhalla]]/[[Vanir]] guilds

articles.body:
## Background

The Mage Legacy and TheNoLifes were both [[Valhalla]] members from its founding on 11 May 2021, part of the thirteen-guild bloc that took the map after [[The Great Collapse]]{{cite:community-guild-timeline|11 May 2021 Valhalla roster}}. Friction between the two and their allies appears from August 2021, months before any open break{{cite:territory-exchanges|Mage Legacy and TheNoLifes friction from August 2021}}.

## The betrayal

When Valhalla's guilds reorganized as [[Vanir]] on 28 Nov 2021, both were excluded{{cite:community-guild-timeline|28 Nov 2021 Vanir roster}}. Open war followed in December: 5,359 territory exchanges that month between the two betrayers and their former allies — one of the most violent single months of territory warfare on record{{cite:territory-exchanges|5,359 territory exchanges, December 2021}}.

TheNoLifes went on to help lead [[Khaos]]{{cite:cameron-oral-history|Cameron oral history (TAq veteran testimony)}}, which it joined around 1 December 2021{{cite:chronicle-records|Khaos membership: TheNoLifes from ~1 Dec 2021}}.

{{map:2021-11-28|The map when Vanir formed without the betrayers}}

## Aftermath

By early 2022 the fighting had folded into [[khaos-s-last-war|Khaos's last war]], the winter-long struggle between Khaos and the ex-Valhalla guilds. TheNoLifes stayed hostile to its former allies into 2023, long after the blocs themselves had dissolved{{cite:territory-exchanges|TheNoLifes' hostility to the ex-Valhalla guilds persisting into 2023}}.

articles.title: The Diplomacy update
articles.summary: Wynncraft's in-game guild ally system, introduced in version 1.20 (2021). Allying is a game-mechanical relationship — an ally tax rate, and from 2026 the ability for allied guilds to run Guild Raids together — rather than a political alliance, though from June 2026 its events became the first machine-readable record of guild relationships.

infobox.label: What allying does
infobox.value: Applies the ally tax rate; from 2026, permits joint Guild Raids

infobox.label: API status
infobox.value: No alliance field in the official API (as of Sep 2026)

articles.body:
Wynncraft has had an in-game guild ally system since version 1.20 'Gavel Reborn' (20 January 2021){{cite:thread-281822|post #1, 20 Jan 2021}}{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Guilds & Wars' sections, 23 Nov 2020}}. Allying is a game-mechanical status rather than a declaration: it interacts with the [[territory-warfare|territory system]] through the ally tax rate charged on an allied guild's territories{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-war|attack-cost formula: allied guilds are charged the ally tax}}, and a Diplomacy menu in the guild UI lists a guild's allies (up to 16, per the Sequoia mod's snapshot feature){{cite:github-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod-blob-main-src-test-java-com-seq|GuildAllianceSnapshotManagerTest}}. Setting a guild as an ally does not indicate a political alliance — allied guilds may be rivals or recent belligerents — and the in-game menu played no recorded part in the [[the-realignment-era|realignment-era]] or [[private-diplomacy-era|private-diplomacy-era]] blocs.

What the system is chiefly for became explicit in 2026. Version 2.2.1 (12 June 2026) added the change 'Guild Allies can now do Guild Raids together'{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-2-2-1|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Version 2.2.1' (12 Jun 2026)}}, which is the point of the feature as it is used: two guilds register as allies so that their members can run guild raids as one group. The feature is also dated to version 2.2.2 of 10 July 2026{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}; the wiki's changelogs attribute it to 2.2.1{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-2-2-2|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Version 2.2.2' (10 Jul 2026)}}.

The same month, [[Sequoia]]'s open-source client mod began parsing the in-game 'formed/revoked an alliance with' chat broadcasts (commit of 12 June 2026){{cite:github-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod|commit 69fb472, 12 Jun 2026}}, the first such records made by software rather than written down by a person{{cite:raw-githubusercontent-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod-main-src-test-java-com-seqwawa-|ChatManagerTest alliance-message fixtures}}. From 30 July 2026 the mod auto-snapshots the Diplomacy menu to Sequoia's private backend, a growing machine-readable archive that is not publicly accessible{{cite:github-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod|commit 8b27368 and Modrinth 1.8.0 changelog, 30 Jul 2026}}. The official API exposed no alliance field as of 2 September 2026{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-sequoia|v3/guild response, retrieved 2 Sep 2026}}, so the in-game record remains readable only through such tooling.
articles.leadImageCaption: In-game 'View Diplomacy' tooltip shown in the 1.20 'Gavel Reborn' changelog: a guild's alliance list naming two allied guilds.

articles.title: The Economy Update
articles.summary: Wynncraft version 1.18, the Economy Update, released 18 January 2019: professions, crafting and an in-game trade market. It reshaped the economy that funded guilds but left war mechanics essentially untouched.

infobox.label: Focus
infobox.value: Professions (gathering and crafting), trade market, guild banners

articles.body:
Version 1.18, officially titled 'The Economy Update', was released on 18 January 2019{{cite:thread-238340|Wynncraft forums thread 238340, '1.18 The Economy Update - Changelog'}}{{cite:https://wynncraft.fandom.com/wiki/Version_1.18|Wynncraft Wiki (Fandom), 'Version 1.18'}} — between the [[the-federation-dies|Federation's fall]] and the founding of [[Luna]], in the middle of [[the-alliance-wars-of-2019|the alliance wars of 2019]].

Its focus was the player economy rather than warfare: it introduced the professions system (gathering and crafting){{cite:thread-238340|Wynncraft forums thread 238340, '1.18 The Economy Update - Changelog'}}, and it added the in-game Trade Market{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-version-1-18|Trade Market listed under the 1.18 additions}}. The feature was trailed in January 2019 on the official Twitter account; the announcement itself does not survive{{cite:x-com-wynncraft-status-1084983171920351232-wb20251203|the status URL captured 3 Dec 2025 returns an empty page}}. On the guild side its contribution was cosmetic: 1.18 introduced guild banners, replacing 'the Mysterious Potatoes riddle'{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guilds|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Guilds' (trivia)}}.

No changes to the guild war system itself were recorded in 1.18. The economy-and-war rework that transformed [[territory-warfare|territory warfare]] — war towers, guild resource production, trade routes and taxation — came two years later, in version 1.20 'Gavel Reborn' (20 January 2021){{cite:thread-281822|post #1, 20 Jan 2021}}{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Guilds & Wars' sections, 23 Nov 2020}}, which also laid the groundwork for [[guild-seasons|Guild seasons]] and the in-game ally system (see [[the-diplomacy-update|The Diplomacy update]]).
articles.leadImageCaption: Official logo for Wynncraft version 1.18, the Economy Update, released 18 January 2019.

articles.title: The Federation
articles.summary: The Federation was the dominant Wynncraft war alliance of 2018, founded around 16 Feb 2018 out of the Coalition remnant and the War Syndicate remains, and led by Drew1011. It took the entire territory map on 21 Feb 2018 and held it for 8 months and 25 days, grew to 37-40 member guilds, and died by internal collapse in a single day on 10 Nov 2018.

infobox.label: Map control from
infobox.value: 21 Feb 2018 (356 of 383 territories); the opposing bloc was eliminated on 19–20 Mar 2018

articles.title: The Federation dies
articles.summary: The internal collapse of the Federation on 10 November 2018: one guild left at around 3 AM EST, and the alliance that had held the entire map for 8 months and 25 days cascaded apart within a day.

infobox.label: Alliance
infobox.value: [[the-federation|Federation]] (and the [[Aesir Pact]], which died with it)

infobox.label: Cause
infobox.value: Internal collapse — 'what killed Federation was... internal affairs' (Drew1011)

articles.body:
The death of the [[the-federation|Federation]] on 10 November 2018 ended the longest period of total map control in the recorded history of Wynncraft guild warfare. The alliance was not defeated from outside: one guild's departure at around 3 AM EST triggered a cascade that emptied it within a day{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}.

{{map:2018-11-10|The map on the day of the collapse}}

## Background

The Federation formed around 16 February 2018 from the merger of the [[Coalition]] remnant and War Syndicate's remains, founded and led by [[Drew1011]]{{cite:thread-265297|post #16, Lego_DW, 4 Apr 2020}}. It wiped [[HackForums]] on 19 February, won the [[coalition-civil-war|Coalition Civil War]] on 20 March{{cite:community-guild-timeline|19 Feb and 20 Mar 2018 entries}}, and then held the entire map for 8 months and 25 days, interrupted only for roughly three days in March. At its height it counted 37–40 member guilds{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}.

Strain had shown all year. [[Fantasy]] left in late May 2018 and fought the bloc across the map all summer — over 220 territories were exchanged{{cite:territory-exchanges|220+ territories exchanged with Federation guilds, summer 2018}} — before rejoining on 29 October{{cite:community-guild-timeline|29 Oct 2018 entry}}. The Hive left about a month before the end, then Odysseia{{cite:thread-236962|post #17, Ascended Kitten, 11 Nov 2018}}. Several separate wars between member guilds ignited on 1 November 2018: the pre-collapse fraying{{cite:territory-exchanges|intra-Federation wars igniting 1 Nov 2018}}.

## The collapse

At around 3 AM EST on 10 November 2018 one guild left the Federation, and the rest cascaded out within a day{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}. [[Imperial]]'s exit 'snowballed into a major attack together with the enemy alliance', Ascended Kitten of Imperial wrote the next day; Arisen followed; and after 14 hours of constant warring the [[Aesir Pact]] guilds — Sins of Seedia, [[DiamondDeities]] and IceBlue Team, the Federation's last defenders — quit, ending it{{cite:thread-236962|post #17, Ascended Kitten, 11 Nov 2018}}. The Aesir Pact died with the alliance it defended.

Drew1011 posted a tribute three days later: 'What killed Federation was... internal affairs.'{{cite:thread-237070|post #1, 13 Nov 2018}}

## Aftermath

The community timeline describes the winter 2018–19 interregnum simply: 'After Fed all guilds keep to themselves with valk owning most of Gavel'{{cite:thread-265297|post #1, the community guild-timeline image}} — [[Valkyrie]]'s guilds, Kingdom Foxes and Imperial, were the interregnum's top territory gainers{{cite:territory-exchanges|top territory gainers, winter 2018–19}}. [[sol|SOL]] was created in the post-collapse chaos, and [[Luna]] formed on 14 February 2019 to counter it{{cite:community-guild-timeline|14 Feb 2019 entry}}, opening [[the-alliance-wars-of-2019|the alliance wars of 2019]].

articles.title: The forum megalist
articles.summary: Wynncraft forums thread 278112, created and maintained by Sg_Voltage from 29 November 2020: the community-maintained list of guilds and alliances. Its posts of December 2020 - June 2022 preserve most of the era's known alliance rosters; its alliance section was deleted on 7 July 2022, ending public alliance rosters.
articles.body:
Between December 2020 and June 2022 it was the only public, dated record of who was allied with whom - and nearly every known alliance roster of the [[artemis-goose-era|Artemis-Goose]] and [[the-realignment-era|realignment]] eras traces to one of its posts.

## Authorship

The thread was created on 29 November 2020 by [[sg-voltage|Sg_Voltage]], who maintained it for years afterwards{{cite:thread-278112|thread opened 29 Nov 2020; Sg_Voltage replies through p1}}. Pally - [[paladinsorcerer|PaladinSorcerer]] of [[Titans Valor]] - was a reader, and the author of the thread's 2 December 2020 alliance post{{cite:thread-278112|p1 #10, Pally, 2 Dec 2020}}, but never its maintainer. Sg_Voltage's own guild affiliation is unknown; his forum profile displayed a CHAMPION rank and no guild{{cite:thread-278112-wb20210704|post #1, capture of 4 Jul 2021}}.

The opening post set out the project - 'I've assembled a list of every* guild which is currently recruiting along with some important stats for each ... My goal is to be able to make sure every guild gets the chance to shine' - and the listing itself lived in a Google Sheet edited by the guilds themselves: 'If you're a high ranking member of a guild and want to see your guild added or want to make changes, send me a message with your Gmail and I'll give you editing permission.' One of the sheet's columns was Alliances - 'Some guilds are in alliances for warring, this is where they're listed' - and that column is why the thread matters to guild history{{cite:thread-278112-wb20210704|post #1, capture of 4 Jul 2021}}. After Sg_Voltage was asked whether he intended to update it weekly, forum administrator colin350 pinned the thread on 17 January 2021{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #65 and #67, colin350, 14-17 Jan 2021}}.

## Landmark posts

Its landmark entries include: the 2 December 2020 post by Pally (post #10) recording that 'ANO is apart of the alliances Hestia (a community alliance between ANO, ESI, LXA, and PUN) and Artemis (war alliance) made up of all the current massive land holding guilds on the map'{{cite:thread-278112|p1 #10, Pally, 2 Dec 2020}} - the first record of both [[Hestia]] and [[Artemis]]; two posts on the morning of 19 January 2021, 99loulou999's 'TNR (TNI and TNA) are part of Goose' and Lev98bug's 'Eden is in Goose if you could add that', the earliest recorded uses of the name [[Goose]], to which Sg_Voltage replied 'Just want to drop in and say that I'm a huge fan of the name'{{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #71-73, 19 Jan 2021}}; the 1 February 2021 side-switch report by urbymine ('BNU(IBT), SHY and TNL are all goose now'){{cite:thread-278112-p04|p4 #76, urbymine, 1 Feb 2021}}; the 25 May 2021 post recording the [[Valhalla]]/[[Khaos]] renames after [[the-great-collapse|the Great Collapse]]{{cite:thread-278112-p07|p7 #134-137, 25 May 2021}}; Pally's six-guild Hestia roster of 6 June 2021{{cite:thread-278112-p07|p7 #140, Pally, 6 Jun 2021}}; the 7 July 2021 [[Niflheim]] roster{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #146, HungHung, 7 Jul 2021}}; and the 26 June 2022 post giving [[Cucumber Company]]'s full 14-guild roster{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #160, TherapueticLiz, 26 Jun 2022}} - the last public alliance roster ever posted anywhere.

## The deletion

Twelve days later, on 7 July 2022, the thread's alliance section was deleted. Replying to the Cucumber Company roster in post #161, Sg_Voltage first explained that 'for alliance information, it's supposed to be updated by the guilds themselves, I noticed it was out of date so I just moved it to the side. I don't care to follow guild drama', then added: 'You know what, on second thought I'm just going to delete that section. If it's not updated regularly it's not really useful anyways.'{{cite:thread-278112-p09|p9 #161, Sg_Voltage, 7 Jul 2022}} The deletion marks the boundary between the public record and [[private-diplomacy-era|the private diplomacy era]]: no alliance roster has been published since{{cite:thread-278112-wb20220517|capture of 17 May 2022, alliance column still described in the opening post}}{{cite:thread-278112-wb20220915|capture of 15 Sep 2022, alliance column gone}}.

The thread itself outlived its alliance column. Sg_Voltage reported the sheet being flagged by Google in January 2023 and was still fielding update requests that March, and readers were still posting to it in 2025{{cite:thread-278112-p09|p9 #168 and #170, Jan-Mar 2023; #172-174, 2025}}. The underlying Google Sheet was never captured by any web archive, so the Valhalla- and Khaos-era rosters it once held are gone from the public web{{cite:chronicle-records|the lost Google Sheet; megalist authorship correction}}; the thread's posts survive partly through Wayback Machine snapshots{{cite:thread-278112-wb20210704|post #1, capture of 4 Jul 2021}}.

articles.title: The Great Collapse
articles.summary: On 11 May 2021, Goose and Artemis — the two blocs that had fought the war for the map — both collapsed on the same day. Thirteen guilds formed Valhalla and nine formed Khaos, and the new blocs went straight to war.
articles.body:
The Great Collapse is the name given to 11 May 2021, the day [[Goose]] and [[Artemis]] both collapsed and the guild world reorganized into [[Valhalla]] and [[Khaos]]{{cite:community-guild-timeline|11 May 2021 entry}} — ending the [[artemis-goose-era|Artemis-Goose era]] and beginning the Valhalla one.

{{map:2021-05-11|The map on the day of the collapse}}

## Background

The [[goose-artemis-war|Goose-Artemis war]] had run since December 2020{{cite:thread-279337|post #1, Sheepn, 18 Dec 2020}}: Artemis the map-holder, Goose the coalition that rose against it and eventually took map control. By May 2021 Goose had absorbed much of the old Artemis world along with the guilds that would become Khaos's core.

## The collapse

On 11 May 2021 both alliances dissolved on the same day. Thirteen guilds — including [[The Aquarium]] — formed Valhalla, while nine, largely the Goose bloc's core (Aequitas, Wheres The Finish, Nerfuria, Ultra Violet, Fuzzy Spiders, ChinaNumberOne, Cyphrus Code, Eden, with Tartarus Wrath joining days later), formed Khaos{{cite:community-guild-timeline|11 May 2021 rosters}}. Valhalla took map control from Goose's remnants within days{{cite:community-guild-timeline|the May 2021 entry: Valhalla takes map control from Goose}}.

A megalist post of 25 May 2021 recorded that 'the two major alliances both disbanded and got new names... Valhalla and Kaos', while noting that [[Valkyrie]] 'stayed the same'{{cite:thread-278112-p07|post #134, Dream, 25 May 2021}}{{cite:thread-278112-p07|post #136, Dream, 25 May 2021}}. No public rosters of the new blocs were ever posted{{cite:community-guild-timeline|11 May 2021 rosters}}. Why both alliances fell on the same day is not recorded.

## Aftermath

The [[valhalla-khaos-war|Valhalla-Khaos war]] began the day both blocs formed and outlived them both in their original shapes. The collapse also fixed the shape of guild politics for the following year: Valhalla's line ran through [[Vanir]] to the great 2022 realignment{{cite:chronicle-records|Goose, Artemis, Valhalla and Khaos}}, and Khaos's guilds were eventually absorbed into [[Cucumber Company]]{{cite:thread-278112-p08|post #160, TherapueticLiz, 26 Jun 2022}}.

articles.title: The Guild Update
articles.summary: Guilds and guild wars were introduced to Wynncraft in version 1.13, the Wynnter Update, released on 22 December 2014 — the starting point of all guild warfare history.
articles.body:
Guilds were introduced to Wynncraft in version 1.13 — the 'Wynnter Update' — released on 22 December 2014{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guilds|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Guilds'}}{{cite:https://wynncraft.fandom.com/wiki/Version_1.13|Wynncraft Wiki (Fandom), 'Version 1.13'}}, and guild wars have existed since the same update{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-war|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Guild War'}}. Per the official wiki, guilds 'were originally going to just be permanent parties'{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guilds|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Guilds'}}; instead they became territorial powers, and the war system introduced here is the one under which the entire [[early-guild-era|early guild era]] and [[federation-era|Federation era]] were fought.

In the original system, players accessed the Guild Master through a teleporter in Troms (moved to the Guild Hall in the 1.14 Gavel expansion of 2015){{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guilds|Official Wynncraft Wiki, 'Guilds'}}. The 1.13-era war mechanics — including mob-wave wars fought on dedicated war servers, with territories generating XP — survived with incremental changes for six years, until the ground-up rework in version 1.20 'Gavel Reborn' (20 January 2021{{cite:thread-281822|post #1, 20 Jan 2021}}{{cite:thread-277744|post #1, 'Guilds & Wars' sections, 23 Nov 2020}}; see [[territory-warfare|Territory warfare]] and [[guild-seasons|Guild seasons]]).

Every era article on this wiki descends from this update: the first territorial powers of 2015–2016, the [[HackForums]] dominance, and everything after (see [[history-of-wynncraft-guild-warfare|History of Wynncraft guild warfare]]).
articles.leadImageCaption: A tier 1 guild banner, the customisable emblem each guild carries.

articles.title: The Long Raid
articles.summary: A roughly week-long siege of Aequitas's claim in the Sky province, late July to early August 2024 - the only battle of its era with a first-person retelling, the video 'Wynncraft Warring - The Long Raid' by Frank Wynncraft. The attackers were never named, and the outcome is not known.

infobox.label: Dates
infobox.value: late Jul - early Aug 2024 (~28 Jul - 4 Aug)

articles.body:
The retelling that makes it the only documented battle of [[private-diplomacy-era|its era]] is the video 'Wynncraft Warring - The Long Raid' by Frank Wynncraft, which premiered on 4 August 2024{{cite:youtube-com-watch-v-rlrh14ns6ok|premiered 4 Aug 2024}}, followed by a forum post of 9 August 2024 in which Defervesco linked it - '[[Aequitas]]'s claim in sky was under siege for some time last week. Enjoy this retelling of the war!'{{cite:thread-318070|post #1, Defervesco, 9 Aug 2024}}

{{map:2024-07-28|The map during the siege}}

## Background

The raid falls inside the window of the [[idiot-co-aquarium-war|Idiot Co-Aquarium war]], the era's dominant conflict{{cite:territory-exchanges|Idiot Co-Aquarium war window, Apr–Jul 2024}}, but is described in the retelling as small-guild warfare rather than part of that war's main front{{cite:youtube-com-watch-v-rlrh14ns6ok|premiered 4 Aug 2024}}.

## Course of the war

The attackers besieged Aequitas's Sky-province claim for about a week{{cite:territory-exchanges|siege window, ~28 Jul – 4 Aug 2024}}. The attackers were never named, and the outcome was not recorded.

## Aftermath

Nothing further is recorded. The video is a rare first-person account from a period when almost all guild diplomacy and war reporting had moved to private channels.

'Wynncraft Warring' is not a series: of the thirteen videos on Frank Wynncraft's channel, only this one carries the title{{cite:chronicle-records|section 6: Frank Wynncraft channel enumeration from the Wayback capture of 8 May 2026}}. The rest are build, market, raid and update videos.
articles.leadImageCaption: Thumbnail of Frank Wynncraft's video 'Wynncraft Warring - The Long Raid', premiered 4 August 2024.

articles.title: The Mage Legacy
articles.summary: Wynncraft guild created in October 2016 and led by CalAnders ever since — one of the longest unbroken guild ownerships on record. It joined Goose in March 2021, was a founding member of Valhalla, and was one of the two guilds excluded when Valhalla reorganized as Vanir.
articles.body:
The Mage Legacy's owner, CalAnders, joined at the moment of the guild's creation and was still its owner in September 2026 — an unbroken tenure of nearly ten years, and one of the longest on record{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-the-20mage-20legacy|v3/guild response, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}.

## History

### The Emperium of Wynn (2017)

The Mage Legacy first appears as an alliance member in the [[emperium-of-wynn|Emperium of Wynn]], listed as 'The Mage Legacy (Mag) - Owner: CalAnders' among the alliance's current guilds in May 2017{{cite:thread-188024|post #4 (quoting the OP as it then stood), 7 May 2017}}; by August 2017 the guild had been moved to the alliance's 'Honored Retired Guilds' list{{cite:thread-188024|post #1 (OP), 'Honored Retired Guilds', as of 8 Aug 2017}}. CalAnders himself posted in the thread on the day it opened{{cite:thread-188024|post #5, 7 May 2017}}. Nothing more was recorded of the guild for almost four years.

### Goose and Valhalla (2021)

The Mage Legacy joined [[Goose]] on 30 March 2021, during the [[goose-artemis-war|Goose-Artemis war]]{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. That same day [[drasalia|Drasalia]] of ChinaNumberOne posted an illustrated roster of six Goose guilds headed 'MAG - The Mage Legacy' — 'just my doodles of what I think the Guilds would look like if they were people'{{cite:thread-289196|post #1, 30 Mar 2021}}.

When Goose and [[Artemis]] fell together on 11 May 2021 ([[the-great-collapse|the Great Collapse]]), The Mage Legacy was one of the thirteen founding guilds of [[Valhalla]], the bloc that took the map from Goose's remnants{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}.

### Excluded from Vanir

Friction between The Mage Legacy, [[thenolifes|TheNoLifes]] and their Valhalla allies appears from August 2021, months before any open break{{cite:territory-exchanges|Mage Legacy and TheNoLifes friction from August 2021}}. Both guilds were left out when Valhalla's remaining members reorganized as [[Vanir]] on 28 November 2021, and open war followed that December ([[the-betrayal-of-valhalla|the betrayal of Valhalla]]){{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. Where The Mage Legacy went afterwards was never recorded; unlike TheNoLifes, which passed into [[Khaos]], it appears in no later alliance roster.

As of September 2026 the guild remains active at level 90 with 87 members and 13,368 recorded wars, holding no territories{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-the-20mage-20legacy|v3/guild response, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}.

## Alliances

- [[emperium-of-wynn|Emperium of Wynn]] — by 7 May 2017; a retired guild by August 2017{{cite:thread-188024|post #4 and post #1 (OP), 2017}}
- [[Goose]] — 30 Mar – 11 May 2021
- [[Valhalla]] — 11 May – 28 Nov 2021 (founding member)

articles.title: The Nameless Samurai
articles.summary: A Wynncraft guild created in September 2023 that held 59 of the map's 437 territories in the census of 3 September 2026 - level with Avicia and behind only Sequoia. No forum thread, newsletter, video or narrative account of it was ever written; two API captures are the whole of its record.
articles.body:
The Nameless Samurai [TNSR] is a Wynncraft guild created on 28 September 2023{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-the-20nameless-20samurai|guild record, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}. On 3 September 2026 it held 59 of the map's 437 territories - level with [[Avicia]] and behind only [[Sequoia]]'s 62{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-list-territory|full territory ownership snapshot, 3 Sep 2026}}. It is among the largest territorial powers ever recorded, and no forum thread, newsletter, video or narrative account of it was ever written. Two API captures are the whole of its record.

## What the record contains

The guild's API record of 3 September 2026 lists makugon as owner and ten chiefs - _Snowy_, pozicoco, yayo_dayo, sutiru_, DOBUMASUO, nasinasi820, suraimu1233301, aoiei, tamago_256 and xX_ThinkiFace_Xx - across 84 members at guild level 77, with 12,345 lifetime wars and 1,979 raids{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-the-20nameless-20samurai|owner, chiefs, member total, level and lifetime counts, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}.

Those figures sit oddly beside its holdings. Of the six largest holders in the census it has the fewest members, the lowest guild level, and by an order of magnitude the fewest lifetime wars. [[Avicia]], on the same 59 territories, records 227,706 wars{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-avicia|lifetime war count, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}; [[Sequoia]] records 161,494{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-sequoia|lifetime war count, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}; [[KongoBoys]], on roughly half the territory, records 98,864{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-kongoboys|lifetime war count, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}}. How a guild with a five-figure war count came to hold as much land as one with a six-figure war count was never documented.

The season record says the same thing from the other side. The guild's season ratings run from Season 14 (1,300) through Season 32 (590,577), peaking at 2,416,820 in Season 24{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-the-20nameless-20samurai|seasonRanks, retrieved 3 Sep 2026}} - roughly a fifth of the totals that won seasons over the same years, which ran between 10 and 14.6 million{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season winners table, Seasons 19-25}}. By season rating the guild was never a contender for a crown; by territory count it was second on the map.

## The claim

The 59 territories formed a single regional bloc in central Gavel rather than a scattered holding: the guild's headquarters was Cinfras Outskirts, and the claim ran through Cinfras and its approaches, the Aldorei valley, Gelibord, Lexdale, Thanos, Kander, Efilim and the Forgery{{cite:api-wynncraft-com-v3-guild-list-territory|TNSR territory list and HQ, 3 Sep 2026}}. No written source describes the guild's holdings.

## An undocumented power

No other record of the period mentions the guild. It has no recruitment or guild thread on the Wynncraft forums: of the eleven guild threads of substance posted between 2023 and 2026, none is TNSR's{{cite:chronicle-records|section 9, forum tag sweeps recorded as complete}}. It is named in none of the twenty-one volumes of [[titan-times|Titan Times]], the era's only regularly published newsletter{{cite:chronicle-records|section 8, Titan Times vols. 14-21 name no outside guild}}, and in none of the in-game chat records captured by [[Sequoia]]'s client mod in 2026{{cite:raw-githubusercontent-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod-main-src-test-java-com-seqwawa-|ChatManagerTest fixtures}}. No war involving it is recorded, no alliance, no leadership change, no founding account and no disband notice. Nobody wrote it down.

That absence is the ordinary condition of [[private-diplomacy-era|the private-diplomacy era]], in which the last alliance thread on the forums is dated 21 November 2022 and guild politics moved into private Discords{{cite:thread-322643|post #1, IceResistance, 2 Oct 2025}}. The Nameless Samurai is the sharpest single case of it: a guild founded ten months after that last thread, which reached the top of the map entirely inside the silence.

Its nearest parallel is ten years earlier. [[Libertas]] held 60 of roughly 332 territories on 23 September 2016, second only to [[HackForums]], and its scale was likewise recorded only once{{cite:pre2018-territory-snapshots|pre2018-territory-snapshots.json — Wayback Machine capture of the Wynncraft v1 API guild leaderboard, 23 Sep 2016}}; not one of its wars was ever written down. The two cases bracket the record: at its start and at its present end, a first-rank territorial power exists as a number and almost nothing else.

## Alliances

None recorded. The Nameless Samurai appears in no recorded war or community alliance, and its founding postdates the last public alliance roster by more than a year{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #160, TherapueticLiz, 26 Jun 2022}}. Nor does it appear in the in-game ally records captured from June 2026 - a game-mechanical registration used chiefly to permit allied guilds to run guild raids together{{cite:raw-githubusercontent-com-sequoiawynncraft-sequoia-mod-main-src-test-java-com-seqwawa-|ChatManagerTest alliance-message fixtures}}.

articles.title: The realignment era
articles.summary: May 2021 to mid-2023: Valhalla and Khaos rose from the Great Collapse and fought for a year, Vanir lived twenty days, and the 2022 realignment merged both worlds into Cucumber Company - later smtn elf - until The Aquarium and Avicia walked out in June 2023.
articles.body:
{{map:2022-05-01|The map as Cucumber Company formed}}

The realignment era began with two blocs at war, the survivors of [[the-great-collapse|the Great Collapse]], and ended with nearly all of them inside [[smtn elf]] — the last era with a public alliance record. It is also the first era with a published scoreboard: [[guild-seasons|guild seasons]] launched on 5 July 2021{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|Season 0, 5-7 Jul 2021}}, eight weeks into it, and from then on the map's politics can be read against a table of winners.

## Valhalla and Khaos

On 11 May 2021 thirteen guilds including [[The Aquarium]] formed [[Valhalla]] while nine ex-[[Goose]] guilds formed [[Khaos]]{{cite:thread-278112-p07|p7 #134-137, 25 May 2021}}, and the [[valhalla-khaos-war|Valhalla-Khaos war]] began the same day{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. Valhalla took map control within days and dominated the year - 'the meta of being top 10 on the guild sr leaderboard is to join valhalla', a September 2021 forum post complained{{cite:thread-295680|post #1, IamFye, 25 Sep 2021}}. Fighting was sustained at roughly a thousand exchanges a week at its peaks, continuing into spring 2022{{cite:territory-exchanges|Valhalla-Khaos weekly exchange volumes, 2021-22}}.

The season table bears the complaint out only partly. Season 1 (9 Jul - 20 Sep 2021) went to [[ShadowFall]], Season 2 to [[Emorians]], Season 3 to The Aquarium, Season 4 to Nefarious Ravens{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season table, Seasons 1-4}} - four different winners in a year, three of them Valhalla-line guilds and the first of them a guild that had defected from [[Artemis]] to Goose eight months earlier.

## Betrayal and the twenty days of Vanir

In late 2021 The Mage Legacy and TheNoLifes turned on their Valhalla allies - friction visible from August, erupting into open war in December (5,359 territory exchanges that month){{cite:territory-exchanges|December 2021 territory exchanges}}. Both were excluded when ten Valhalla guilds reorganized as [[Vanir]] on 28 November 2021{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. Vanir lasted twenty days: on 18 December [[Emorians]], Nefarious Ravens, IceBlue Team and [[Avicia]] left and it collapsed; [[Niflheim]] officially dissolved the same day{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}. Khaos's war against the ex-Valhalla guilds - its opponents known as the Pineapple Pact, a name never written down at the time{{cite:cameron-oral-history|Cameron (TAq veteran) oral testimony, fact-checked against map data}} - peaked in January 2022 at 500-800 territory exchanges per week and faded to nothing by mid-July{{cite:territory-exchanges|Khaos war volumes, Jan-Jul 2022}}.

## Cucumber Company and smtn elf

The 2022 realignment merged the ex-Valhalla and ex-Khaos worlds into [[Cucumber Company]], formed for guild Season 5 - 'our first season being a part of the new Cucumber Company war alliance', wrote [[titan-times|Titan Times]]{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol1|vol. 1, 8 May 2022}}. Season 5 ran from 3 March to 2 May 2022{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season table, Season 5}}. Its 14-guild roster, posted to [[the-forum-megalist|the forum megalist]] on 26 June 2022{{cite:thread-278112-p08|p8 #160, TherapueticLiz, 26 Jun 2022}}, was the last public alliance roster ever; the megalist's alliance section was deleted twelve days later{{cite:thread-278112-p09|p9 #161, Sg_Voltage, 7 Jul 2022}}. At the start of Season 8, which began on 12 September 2022{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season table, Season 8}}, 'Cucumber was archived. The new alliance name is called Smtn else' - the same newsletter recording Gang of Fools having 'left and betrayed the alliance' and welcoming [[Paladins United]], [[The Simple Ones]] and TerraLune{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol6|vol. 6, 12 Oct 2022}}. Renamed 'smtn elf' for Christmas 2022 and never changed back{{cite:cameron-oral-history|Cameron (TAq veteran) oral testimony, fact-checked against map data}}, the super-alliance was crowned - satirically - 'unquestionably the greatest super-alliance of 2023' that February{{cite:thread-306790|Wynncraft forums thread 306790, 17 Feb 2023}}. In spring 2023 busted moments and [[Idiot Co]] joined{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol9|vol. 9, 25 Mar 2023}}. Meanwhile the community layer turned over: as [[Hestia]] declined, the leaders of [[Titans Valor]] and Empire of Sindria founded [[Adonis]] around May 2022 as its effective successor{{cite:titantimes-github-io-vol1|vol. 1, 8 May 2022}}.

Under the super-alliance the crown circulated among its own members - The Aquarium in Season 5, KongoBoys in Season 6, [[Avicia]] in Season 7, The Aquarium again in Season 8 - and then stopped circulating. Avicia won Seasons 9 through 13 without a break, from October 2022 to August 2023{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season table, Seasons 5-13}}, a run that begins inside smtn elf and ends after it.

## The Eden coup

Somewhere in this period [[Eden]], a founding guild of Khaos, was overthrown from within. A player called xK6TA, applying to [[Titans Valor]] in April 2023, wrote: 'I was a part of Eden when it was #1 and slightly after it got couped.'{{cite:thread-206094-p97|p97 #1922, 16 Apr 2023}} The coup's actors and date were never recorded, beyond that it happened by April 2023, and what '#1' meant is not known - Eden never won a guild season{{cite:wynncraft-wiki-gg-wiki-guild-seasons|season table, Seasons 0-26}}.

## The end

In June 2023 The Aquarium and Avicia quit smtn elf, rejecting pressure to shrink their claims{{cite:chronicle-records|Chronicle alliance and event records}}, and opened [[the-avocado-split|the Avocado split]] against their former allies. smtn elf was last mentioned in Avicia's season post of 10 June 2023{{cite:thread-308780|Avicia guild thread, season post of 10 Jun 2023}}, in the closing days of the Season 12 it had won; its end was never announced. With it ended the era of publicly named alliances, and [[private-diplomacy-era|the private diplomacy era]] began.
